title: Freeze downstream E05/E07/E09 contracts and treatment-neutral capture (E01 amendment)
description:
## Context

Plan-review reconciliation found that E05, E07, and E09 tasks assume contracts E01 must supply, but Tasks 1–4 closed without freezing all of them. Per the closed ravel-q3w.4 amendment rule, changes to `pilot/e01/` require a new Git revision and content digest before affected runs; this task is that amendment.

This task freezes the remaining downstream contracts and the treatment-neutral measurement capture needed for A/B/C comparability, before any prerequisite epic implements against assumptions.

## Desired State

`pilot/e01/` artifacts (extending `experiments.md` or small sibling files) freeze, to the extent Tasks 1–3 have not already frozen them:

- controller lease duration, renewal cadence, and stop margin;
- the one selected Linux containment mechanism with its mounts/limits/descriptors and the authoritative descendant-quiescence rule;
- path-component grammar, invalid-UTF-8 rule, Unicode normalization version, case/collision-key algorithm, and golden vectors;
- stable target identity, total order, tie behavior, deterministic packing rule, and positive group cap;
- treatment-neutral measurement capture: common run/attempt validity and invalid-attempt replacement rules; timing boundaries and fault placement; run-start and run-terminal records; per-host monotonic busy intervals; work-ready, dispatch, and terminal events; provider usage and cost; final-rediscovery completion; and reserved treatment-C run IDs for qualifying `ravel-85q.8` and `ravel-e1n.7` proofs, each counted as a C observation exactly once.

A new Git revision and content digest are recorded for the amended `pilot/e01/` set; old and amended results are not silently pooled.

## Implementation Guidance

- First audit the closed Tasks 1–3 artifacts (`environment.yaml`, `research.md`, the Task 3 Change contract) and the PR #6 `budgets.yaml`/`experiments.md`; freeze only what is genuinely missing. Do not restate already-frozen values.
- Follow the existing private `pilot/e01/` convention: flat scalars, fixed tables, golden vectors. No schema, validator, framework, or runtime module.
- The capture contract must be treatment-neutral: identical record shapes for A, B, and C so no treatment gains measurement advantage.
- Reserved C run IDs let one qualifying `ravel-85q.8` run and one qualifying `ravel-e1n.7` run count as treatment-C observations exactly once, only when executed under this frozen capture contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Controller lease duration/renewal cadence/stop margin, the selected Linux containment mechanism and authoritative quiescence rule, path grammar/invalid-UTF-8/normalization/collision rules with golden vectors, and stable target identity/order/tie/packing/group-cap rules are frozen in `pilot/e01/` or verified already frozen, with exact locations cited. **(E05/E07/E09 contract dependencies)**
- [ ] Treatment-neutral capture is frozen: run/attempt validity and invalid-attempt replacement, timing boundaries and fault placement, run-start/terminal records, per-host monotonic busy intervals, work-ready/dispatch/terminal events, provider usage/cost, final-rediscovery completion, and reserved C run IDs for qualifying `ravel-85q.8`/`ravel-e1n.7` runs counted exactly once. **(E01 AC6)**
- [ ] A clean-checkout smoke regenerates and revalidates inventory, fixtures, path/collision golden vectors, containment preflight, orthogonal audit, and experiment capture fields; the new Git revision and content digest are recorded outside the hashed directory. **(E01 AC8)**
- [ ] The diff contains only private `pilot/e01/` artifacts; no framework, validator, or runtime module is added. **(E01 AC8)**

## Testing Strategy

- **Manual review:** table/vector review against the E05/E07/E09 task texts that consume each contract.
- **Live integration:** clean-checkout regeneration smoke and digest reproduction as above.

## Design Gate

Amendment authorized by plan-review reconciliation (Findings 6, 9); mechanism per closed ravel-q3w.4 amendment rule. No separate design review required.

## Final Step

- [ ] Run a /ponytail-review pass on the final work (remove over-engineering; simplest version that meets the acceptance criteria) before closing this task.
- [ ] Run a /doc-rigor pass on the final work (verify all docs/comments against source) before closing this task.

title: Execute Hidden Deterministic Evaluation Without Candidate Access to Trust Roots
description:
## Context

E08 requires hidden deterministic commands to evaluate untrusted candidate code without exposing evaluator code, hidden inputs, credentials, or ambient host authority. Read-only mounts are insufficient because candidate-controlled build scripts, proc macros, and binaries could still read and disclose them.

This task implements the narrow local trusted evaluator runner and its immutable four-state evidence. It reuses the Linux isolation and process ownership established by E07 rather than building another sandbox runtime.

## Current State

The repository currently contains only design documents and Beads metadata; no evaluator code exists. This task consumes the trusted action from Step 1, E07's distinct evaluator launch-policy type, owned process group, bounded pipe handling, filesystem isolation, and exact candidate reconstruction, plus E02's immutable artifact storage and E04's attempt/work fence.

Relevant settled design is `docs/mvp-outline.md` §22 and the security-domain rules in §28. Suggested §42 locations are `pi-campaign/src/oracle/runner.rs`, `pi-campaign/src/sandbox/process.rs`, `pi-campaign/src/sandbox/filesystem.rs`, `pi-campaign/src/sandbox/policy.rs`, and `pi-campaign/src/storage/artifacts.rs`.

## Desired State

A concrete trusted evaluator supervisor accepts only a Step 1 action and verified E07 candidate. Evaluator code and hidden inputs remain in a supervisor-only namespace. Candidate-controlled compilation/execution receives only the minimum explicit invocation or artifact interface and cannot enumerate, open, inherit, or disclose the evaluator/hidden roots.

Each run gets a fresh private writable output/temp area and no shared writable build/package/compiler cache. The candidate-controlled subprocess has an allowlisted environment, only required file descriptors, no model/code-host credentials, no credential helpers or agent/daemon sockets, no network, no host service access, and bounded CPU, memory, process, wall-time, filesystem, stdout, and stderr usage.

The supervisor kills and reaps the whole process group before workspace cleanup on timeout, cancellation, crash, blocked output, or runner failure. The trusted parser emits exactly `PASS`, `FAIL`, `ERROR`, or `TIMEOUT`. Each attempt stores new immutable evidence bound to the Step 1 action, candidate, evaluator generation, work revision/fence, bounded redacted output/artifact digests, and resource observations.

## Implementation Guidance

- Keep evaluator and hidden-input roots entirely outside the candidate-visible mount namespace. Do not rely on read-only permissions for secrecy.
- If the evaluator must invoke candidate-controlled compilation or execution, make that a nested restricted subprocess and pass only explicit non-secret files/arguments needed for the operation.
- Start from an empty allowlisted environment. Close every non-required FD, disable inherited Git credential helpers/config and SSH/GPG/agent sockets, and avoid exposing daemon sockets or host paths.
- Bound and continuously drain stdout/stderr. Apply secret/canary redaction before retained output is persisted; never persist unbounded diagnostics.
- Reuse E07 process-group kill/reap and workspace lifecycle code. Do not add a pluggable sandbox backend.
- Use table-driven tests for policy wiring. Reserve end-to-end cases for representative timeout, output saturation, resource breach, and isolation behavior.
- A retry creates a distinct immutable attempt; it never overwrites prior evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The runner accepts only a trusted Step 1 action and verifies the exact E07 candidate identity before execution. (E08 AC2)
- [ ] Evaluator code and hidden inputs are supervisor-only and absent from candidate-visible mounts, FDs, `/proc` paths, environment, and diagnostics. (E08 AC3)
- [ ] Candidate-controlled subprocesses have no model/code-host credentials, helper/agent/daemon sockets, inherited non-required FDs, network, or shared writable cache/state. (E08 AC3, AC6)
- [ ] Every run uses a separate writable area and fixed CPU, memory, process, wall-time, filesystem, and output limits from the trusted action. (E08 AC3)
- [ ] Timeout, cancellation, crash, blocked output, and runner failure kill and reap all descendants before cleanup/reuse. (E08 AC3)
- [ ] The trusted parser yields only immutable `PASS`, `FAIL`, `ERROR`, or `TIMEOUT` evidence with complete subject/evaluator-generation/policy/attempt bindings. (E08 AC2)
- [ ] Repeated attempts create distinct evidence without changing prior evidence. (E08 AC2)
- [ ] Evaluator timeout and crash fault regressions are owned by this component. (E08 AC9)

## Testing Strategy

- **Unit:** table-driven launch-policy wiring for every limit, environment entry, FD rule, network rule, and output bound.
- **Fixture/component:** controlled evaluator fixtures that produce each of the four outcomes and verify complete immutable evidence.
- **Component:** canaries attempt directory enumeration, direct hidden-file reads, `/proc` and inherited-FD reads, environment/helper/agent/socket access, network calls, workspace escape, and output exfiltration; none may expose the canary in retained evidence.
- **Component:** representative timeout, output-saturation, memory/process/filesystem breach, and isolation cases using the real E07 process substrate.
- **Fault:** parent/child processes hold pipes, ignore termination, fork descendants, or crash; all descendants must be reaped before cleanup.
- **Manual review:** verify no second sandbox runtime/backend or shared writable cache was introduced.

## Design Gate
Design settled by docs/mvp-outline.md §21, §22, §23, §24; decomposed from epic ravel-6hv via forged plan /home/ahrav/.claude/plans/2026-08-08-ravel-e08-tasks-v2.md. No separate design review required.

## Final Step

- [ ] Run a /ponytail-review pass on the final work (remove over-engineering; simplest version that meets the acceptance criteria) before closing this task.
- [ ] Run a /doc-rigor pass on the final work (verify all docs/comments against source) before closing this task.

title: Admit Exact Immutable Evidence and Derive the Mechanical Gate
description:
## Context

Immutable evidence is trustworthy only for the exact candidate, evaluator generation, policy, and authorized attempt it evaluated. Local retries and code-host reruns may leave several immutable observations, so the mechanical gate needs an order-independent rule that cannot cherry-pick a `PASS`.

This task adds narrow evidence admission and one flat deterministic reducer. It does not implement semantic judges or a general adjudication subsystem.

## Current State

The repository currently has design documents and Beads metadata but no source code. This task consumes Step 1 action identities, Step 2 immutable local evidence, E03 disposable projections/replay, E04 work revision/fence and sealed submissions, E05 fenced controller commits, and E07 sealed exact-tree/write-policy validation. Step 5 will later supply exact selected-host check-run/run-attempt identities through the same admission seam.

Relevant settled design is `docs/mvp-outline.md` §21-§23. Suggested §42 locations are `pi-campaign/src/domain/evaluation.rs`, `pi-campaign/src/controller/policy.rs`, `pi-campaign/src/sync/event.rs`, and `pi-campaign/src/db/projections.rs`.

## Desired State

Trusted admission verifies the E07 sealed validation identity, current candidate tree/commit, evaluator ID/version, evaluator-generation digest, policy, and authorized work revision/fence. It does not repeat a second full protected-path/tree traversal before dispatch. Remote evidence additionally must match the exact provider check-run and run-attempt identity pinned by the selected-host reader.

Campaign history persists only concrete trusted requirements and immutable observations. The disposable projection derives applicability: local evidence applies only to the requirement's current work revision/fence; remote evidence applies only to its exact pinned provider identity. Other attempts remain inspectable history. Conflicting observations for one supposedly exact identity block regardless of arrival order.

One private function reduces the flat required set: missing or nonterminal evidence is pending; all exact current observations must be `PASS`; any `FAIL`, `ERROR`, `TIMEOUT`, stale identity, or conflicting exact identity is blocked. Existing semantic approval can never override the result.

## Implementation Guidance

- Consume the identity of E07's already sealed exact-tree/write-policy result; do not independently walk every protected path again before dispatch.
- At admission, compare the current trusted evaluator generation once, including workflow/check roots represented in the Step 1 digest.
- Keep requirements and observations as concrete E08 records using E02/E03 event and projection conventions. Do not persist applicability or mechanical-gate events because both are deterministic projections.
- Select the applicable local attempt by current authorized work revision/fence. Select remote evidence by the exact provider check-run/run-attempt identity accepted by the host's required-check API.
- If duplicate bytes for one identity disagree, fail closed as corrupt/conflicting evidence rather than choosing by arrival time or outcome.
- Keep the reducer private in existing evaluation/policy code. Do not create `domain/decision.rs`, `controller/adjudication.rs`, a registry, or a policy engine for this fixed rule.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Admission accepts only evidence matching the current candidate tree/commit, evaluator ID/version, evaluator-generation digest, policy, and authorized attempt identity. (E08 AC2)
- [ ] E07 sealed write-policy/tree validation is identity-checked and trusted evaluator/workflow generation is current at admission. (E08 AC4)
- [ ] Stale or superseded evidence remains immutable history but cannot satisfy a current requirement. (E08 AC2, AC4)
- [ ] Exactly one applicable attempt is derived from current local work revision/fence or pinned remote check-run/run-attempt identity. (E08 AC2)
- [ ] Conflicting `PASS`/non-pass observations produce the same blocked result in every arrival order. (E08 AC2, AC5)
- [ ] Missing/nonterminal evidence is pending, all required `PASS` is pass, and any `FAIL`, `ERROR`, or `TIMEOUT` is blocked. (E08 AC2, AC5)
- [ ] Semantic approval cannot override deterministic blocked/pending state or revive stale evidence. (E08 AC5)
- [ ] History stores requirements and observations only; applicability/gate state is rebuilt in the disposable projection. (E08 AC2, AC10)
- [ ] No general decision/adjudication surface or duplicate protected-path traversal is added. (E08 AC10)

## Testing Strategy

- **Unit:** table of exact and mismatched candidate, evaluator, generation, policy, work revision, fence, and remote check identities.
- **Unit:** flat required-set table for missing, nonterminal, all-pass, fail, error, timeout, stale, and conflicting observations.
- **Unit:** deliver conflicting `PASS`/`FAIL`, `PASS`/`ERROR`, and `PASS`/`TIMEOUT` in both orders and assert identical blocked output.
- **Fixture:** change evaluator policy/generation after an old pass; retain the old observation while deriving it inapplicable.
- **Fixture:** semantic approval beside deterministic non-pass or stale evidence must not become integration-ready.
- **Replay:** rebuild the projection from the same requirements/observations and obtain identical applicability and gate state without stored derived events.
- **Manual review:** verify existing E07 sealed validation is consumed and no new decision/adjudication modules were introduced.

## Design Gate
Design settled by docs/mvp-outline.md §21, §22, §23, §24; decomposed from epic ravel-6hv via forged plan /home/ahrav/.claude/plans/2026-08-08-ravel-e08-tasks-v2.md. No separate design review required.

## Final Step

- [ ] Run a /ponytail-review pass on the final work (remove over-engineering; simplest version that meets the acceptance criteria) before closing this task.
- [ ] Run a /doc-rigor pass on the final work (verify all docs/comments against source) before closing this task.

title: Publish and Reconcile Candidate Refs, the Campaign Branch, and the One Campaign PR
description:
## Context

E08 needs one narrow credentialed publisher for candidate refs, the campaign branch, and the single campaign PR. Network loss makes push and PR outcomes ambiguous; deterministic names alone do not make retries safe, and read-before-retry alone does not prevent a stale publisher from overwriting a competing branch update.

This task implements provider-specific publication and operation-local reconciliation before remote-check admission is added. It makes no custom queue, generic code-host API, or exactly-once claim.

## Current State

The repository currently contains design documents and Beads metadata only. This task builds on E01's selected code host/repository/safe branch policy and exact target base, E04's publisher capability/work identity/fence, E05's fenced history commits and restart handling, E07's exact candidate commit/artifact, and Steps 1 and 3 identities/admission rules.

Relevant settled design is `docs/mvp-outline.md` §24. Suggested §42 locations are `pi-campaign/src/code_host/publisher.rs`, `pi-campaign/src/code_host/state.rs`, `pi-campaign/src/git/candidate.rs`, `pi-campaign/src/git/repository.rs`, `pi-campaign/src/recovery/reconcile.rs`, and `pi-campaign/src/sync/event.rs`.

## Desired State

One concrete selected-host publisher runs only with the literal trusted publisher capability and is the only process receiving code-host credentials. The campaign records its exact target base OID before any write.

Candidate refs have deterministic campaign/candidate names and are created only from expected-absent to the exact E07 commit. The campaign branch and PR head/base derive only from campaign-level inputs. The branch initializes from the recorded base OID, rejects incompatible candidate bases, and every later update atomically changes the exact expected old SHA to the expected new SHA using `force-with-lease` or the selected host's equivalent CAS.

Unknown push outcomes and lease failures reread the exact ref before any retry. Expected new SHA is success, unchanged expected old state permits the same bounded attempt, and any other SHA is a conflict.

Exactly one campaign PR is located by exact provider head/base. Unknown create is retried only if the selected host documents and a live contract test proves an atomic uniqueness/idempotency property. If the first request may still be in flight and lookup returns none, the outcome remains unresolved. Campaign history records candidate ref/SHA, campaign branch/SHA, provider PR ID/head/base, and immutable observations through E04/E05.

## Implementation Guidance

- Call the one host selected by E01 directly. Do not introduce a `CodeHost` trait, backend registry, second provider, generic publication model, or custom CI service.
- Keep credentials in the publisher process only; candidate and evaluator processes must never inherit them through environment, FDs, helpers, agent sockets, diagnostics, or child processes.
- Reuse E04 work identity as the operation identity. Candidate ref plus expected absent/new SHA, campaign ref plus expected old/new SHA, and PR head/base are the external reconciliation keys.
- Do not add a campaign marker, second publication-operation identity, stored PR URL, or known/unknown resolution vocabulary unless the selected host's concrete API cannot reconcile from the minimal keys.
- Implement small concrete reconcilers for candidate ref, campaign branch, and PR. Normal execution and reclaimed/restarted work call the same functions. Do not add a full-world startup reconciler or generic effect/outbox framework.
- On lost response, never issue a blind push. On lease failure, reread before classification.
- For unknown PR create, account for a delayed first request. Query-then-immediate-retry is unsafe without provider-enforced uniqueness/idempotency.
- Keep retries bounded and preserve explicit unresolved work when external state cannot prove the outcome.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Only the trusted publisher process receives code-host credentials; candidate/evaluator environments, FDs, helpers, sockets, and retained output do not contain them. (E08 AC6)
- [ ] The exact campaign target base OID is recorded before publication, branch initialization uses it, and incompatible candidate bases are rejected. (E08 AC7, AC8)
- [ ] Candidate refs are deterministic and create-only from absent to the exact candidate commit. (E08 AC6, AC7)
- [ ] Campaign branch/PR identities depend only on campaign inputs and remain stable when candidates are added or the target branch later moves. (E08 AC7, AC8)
- [ ] Campaign branch updates atomically require the exact expected old SHA; competing writes cannot be overwritten. (E08 AC7)
- [ ] Unknown push outcomes and lease failures reconcile the exact ref before any retry and fail closed on an unexpected SHA. (E08 AC7)
- [ ] PR create/update uses exact head/base; duplicate/unknown create converges only with proven host uniqueness/idempotency and otherwise remains unresolved. (E08 AC7, AC9)
- [ ] Campaign history records candidate ref/SHA, campaign branch/SHA, and provider PR ID/head/base through current fenced E04/E05 authority. (E08 AC6)
- [ ] Restarted/reclaimed work reuses the same per-operation reconciliation and produces no duplicate authoritative publication. (E08 AC7, AC9)
- [ ] No generic host interface, full-world reconciler, custom queue, second PR, or exactly-once claim is introduced. (E08 AC10)

## Testing Strategy

- **Unit:** deterministic identity tests across attempts/restarts; target-branch movement and added candidates cannot change campaign branch/PR identity.
- **Fixture:** exact-base initialization and incompatible-base rejection.
- **Live integration:** create-only candidate ref and exact remote SHA against the selected safe repository.
- **Fault/live integration:** lost response before and after candidate/campaign push success; reread proves state before retry.
- **Race:** insert a competing campaign-branch write between observation and push; lease/CAS fails and reconciliation does not overwrite it.
- **Provider contract:** prove one-open-PR/idempotency behavior for exact head/base, or assert the implementation remains unresolved after an unknown delayed first create. Issue duplicate create/update requests.
- **Restart:** stop the publisher after each external success but before submission/history commit, reclaim the E04 work, and verify one ref transition/PR/authoritative observation.
- **Security/manual review:** credential canaries and dependency/source check for one direct selected-host implementation only.

## Design Gate

title: Read and Admit Existing Remote Required Checks
description:
## Context

The selected code host's existing CI provides heterogeneous remote execution, but a provider-native conclusion becomes Ravel evidence only after trusted code binds it to the exact head, allowlisted workflow/check, issuer, runner labels, evaluator generation, and provider attempt. A runner label proves routing, not isolation.

This task is deliberately read/admit only. All ref mutation and unknown-outcome publication already belongs to Step 4.

## Current State

The repository currently has no source code. This task consumes E01's selected host, fixed required checks/workflow revisions/runner labels, Step 1 trusted action identity, Step 2 evaluator sandbox/interface, Step 3 evidence admission/gate, and Step 4 exact candidate/campaign refs and SHAs.

Relevant settled design is `docs/mvp-outline.md` §21-§24. Suggested §42 locations are `pi-campaign/src/code_host/state.rs`, `pi-campaign/src/domain/evaluation.rs`, `pi-campaign/src/controller/policy.rs`, and `pi-campaign/src/oracle/runner.rs`.

## Desired State

A concrete selected-host reader queries the provider's required-check API for one exact candidate or campaign head SHA. It validates the fixed allowlisted check name/workflow revision, evaluator ID/version, trusted app/issuer, literal runner labels, provider check-run ID, and run-attempt ID. It records only the exact accepted provider identity and immutable mapped observation; it does not mirror provider workflow/run/job state or choose among duplicate runs independently of the host.

One exhaustive mapping covers the selected provider's complete checked-in status/conclusion fixture. Nonterminal is pending. Successful terminal status is `PASS`; deterministic check failure is `FAIL`; provider timeout is `TIMEOUT`; infrastructure, cancellation, and other terminal failure are `ERROR`. New or unknown values fail closed. The observation enters the Step 3 admission seam.

Every allowlisted remote job invokes the same Step 2 evaluator sandbox/minimum interface. Candidate-controlled code cannot access code-host/model tokens, runner registration state, inherited FDs, helper/agent sockets, prior workspaces, local services, evaluator/hidden roots, or shared writable state. Consecutive jobs start clean.

## Implementation Guidance

- Use only the provider-specific API selected by E01. Keep the provider response types at the boundary and map to the four E08 outcomes in one exhaustive match.
- Check in a complete fixture for every provider status/conclusion supported by the pinned client/API version. Unknown decode values or newly added enum cases block until deliberately mapped.
- Nonterminal required checks keep the gate pending; they are not `ERROR` evidence until the provider reports a terminal state.
- Ask the selected host's required-check API which exact check/run attempt is authoritative for the exact head. Record that identity. If the provider response is ambiguous or internally conflicting, block; never choose a passing run by arrival time.
- Validate workflow revision/check name/app issuer/runner labels/head SHA before submitting evidence to Step 3.
- The remote workflow must invoke the existing evaluator runner or an equivalent checked-in entry point using the Step 2 sandbox policy. Do not trust labels as proof of isolation.
- Ensure the job has no candidate-visible code-host/model secrets or persistent self-hosted-runner state. Use clean workspaces and no shared writable cache across trust domains.
- Do not add ref writes, a CI queue, workflow scheduler, generic host interface, or local workflow/run/job state machine.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Required checks are queried and validated at the exact candidate/campaign head SHA. (E08 AC2, AC5)
- [ ] Accepted evidence binds the allowlisted workflow revision/check, evaluator ID/version/generation, trusted issuer/app, exact labels, check-run ID, and run-attempt ID. (E08 AC1, AC2, AC6)
- [ ] The complete selected-provider status space maps exhaustively to pending or `PASS`/`FAIL`/`ERROR`/`TIMEOUT`; new/unknown values fail closed. (E08 AC2)
- [ ] Provider ambiguity/conflict blocks and cannot cherry-pick a passing duplicate run. (E08 AC2, AC5)
- [ ] A check for an old SHA, old evaluator generation/policy, wrong workflow/check/issuer, or wrong labels cannot satisfy the current Step 3 requirement. (E08 AC4, AC9)
- [ ] Existing heterogeneous CI/trusted self-hosted labels execute the fixed required checks; Ravel creates no CI scheduler. (E08 AC1, AC5, AC10)
- [ ] Every remote job uses the evaluator sandbox/interface and exposes no candidate-visible tokens, runner state, FDs, sockets, old workspace, local services, hidden roots, or shared writable state. (E08 AC3, AC6)
- [ ] Consecutive remote jobs cannot read contamination left by the prior job. (E08 AC3)
- [ ] This component performs no ref mutation and introduces no generic host or duplicated CI state model. (E08 AC10)

## Testing Strategy

- **Unit:** exhaustive table over the pinned provider's full status/conclusion fixture, including nonterminal, all terminal categories, and unknown-value failure.
- **Unit/fixture:** exact-head, workflow revision, check name, evaluator generation, issuer/app, labels, check-run, and run-attempt mismatch cases.
- **Fixture:** conflicting/duplicate provider responses cannot select `PASS`; stale pass remains immutable history but Step 3 derives it inapplicable.
- **Live integration:** run every fixed heterogeneous required check on its selected remote/trusted label and retain exact head/workflow/check/issuer/runner/run-attempt IDs.

title: Integrate Current Accepted Candidates Serially and Run the Live Proof
description:
## Context

E08 completes when already accepted non-overlapping candidates advance one campaign branch and one campaign PR serially, while existing required checks and host merge machinery remain authoritative. Mechanical success only permits semantic acceptance; it is not itself an integration decision.

This task wires the completed primitives together and runs one live safe-repository proof. It does not implement semantic judges, overlap analysis, a merge queue, or a second acceptance framework.

## Current State

The repository currently has design documents and Beads metadata but no source. This task consumes E04/E05 fenced work and controller authority, E07 exact candidate artifacts/write-policy identity, Step 3's exact mechanical gate, Step 4's atomic branch/PR publication and operation-local reconciliation, and Step 5's exact required-check evidence.

The accepted-for-integration decision and non-overlap authorization are outputs of controller/Change policy outside this task; E08 only validates they are current and bound to the candidate/evidence. For this task's tests and live smoke, E08 constructs synthetic fixture acceptance/non-overlap records with valid current fences; it does not derive E09 decisions or schedule production candidates. Relevant settled design is `docs/mvp-outline.md` §23-§24. Suggested §42 locations are `pi-campaign/src/git/repository.rs`, `pi-campaign/src/git/candidate.rs`, `pi-campaign/src/code_host/publisher.rs`, `pi-campaign/src/code_host/state.rs`, `pi-campaign/src/controller/scheduler.rs`, and `pi-campaign/src/controller/policy.rs`.

## Desired State

Integration accepts only a current fenced controller decision that identifies the exact candidate, marks it accepted for integration, binds its non-overlap authorization, and references the exact current mechanical evidence. Before each application, trusted code rederives the Step 3 gate and requires all-pass. Missing, stale, or superseded decisions/evidence block. No semantic judge runs here.

One fenced integration job at a time reconstructs the campaign branch at its recorded remote SHA, verifies the E07 candidate artifact/write-policy identity, applies one candidate with trusted Git commands, and updates the branch through Step 4's atomic expected-old reconciler. It records the ordered candidate, resulting commit, branch, and PR observations before another candidate is scheduled.

Step 5 binds required checks to the exact current PR head. Only after those checks pass does Ravel request the selected host's existing merge queue or auto-merge behavior. The one campaign PR stays open while candidates accumulate; per-candidate merge requests do not occur, and production merge timing/completeness is owned by E09 (ravel-e1n.6). Ravel does not plan merge order or replace branch protection.

One gated live smoke command against E01's safe repository applies multiple accepted non-overlapping fixtures to the one branch/PR, exercises actual heterogeneous checks, and proves publisher restart after external success does not duplicate authoritative integration. All fixture candidates accumulate on the one open PR; at most one fixture merge request is issued, after the last application's current-head checks pass. A short source/dependency checklist confirms E08's prohibitions.

## Implementation Guidance

- Require an opaque current controller-authority/fence value when recording or consuming acceptance and integration transitions.
- The acceptance record must bind candidate identity, current mechanical observation identities, and non-overlap authorization. Treat a caller boolean without that fenced record as insufficient.
- Revalidate Step 3 immediately before application; do not cache a prior all-pass result.
- Do not implement semantic-judge execution or overlap detection. Missing upstream acceptance/non-overlap output remains blocked.
- Serialize with existing E04/E05 work/controller mechanisms; do not add a merge planner or queue.
- Use Step 4 exact campaign-branch expected-old/new push and PR identity. After restart/reclaim, invoke the same operation reconciler before repeating any action.
- Record each resulting commit before scheduling the next application. A conflict, unexpected base, protected-path mismatch, or stale identity stops the job.
- Use Step 5 only for the exact current head; prior-head checks cannot authorize merge.
- Keep evaluator, publication, and stale-check fault tests in Steps 2, 4, and 5. Add only one final live smoke, not a duplicate acceptance suite.
- Enforce AC10 with a manual dependency/source/resource checklist rather than automated source-shape assertions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Integration rejects missing, stale, wrong-fence, or superseded accepted-for-integration decisions. (E08 AC8)
- [ ] The accepted decision binds exact candidate identity, non-overlap authorization, and current mechanical observation identities. (E08 AC8)
- [ ] Trusted code rederives the mechanical gate before application; any non-pass/stale evidence blocks even when semantic approval exists. (E08 AC5, AC8)
- [ ] Two or more accepted non-overlapping candidates apply in recorded serial order to one campaign branch and one campaign PR. (E08 AC6, AC8)
- [ ] Each application verifies the E07 artifact/write-policy identity and stops on unexpected base, conflict, protected path, or identity mismatch. (E08 AC4, AC8)
- [ ] Branch updates use Step 4 atomic reconciliation and authoritative history records ordered candidate/resulting commit/branch/PR observations before the next candidate. (E08 AC6-AC8)
- [ ] Only required checks for the exact current PR head can authorize the selected host's existing merge queue/auto-merge path. (E08 AC5, AC8)
- [ ] The campaign PR remains open while candidates accumulate; the live smoke issues at most one merge request after all fixture applications, and no per-candidate merge request occurs. (E08 AC6, AC8)
- [ ] Restart after external branch/PR success but before authoritative history converges without a duplicate candidate application, PR, or integration event. (E08 AC9)
- [ ] One live safe-repository smoke retains exact ref/SHA/check/PR/integration identities and exercises the actual heterogeneous jobs. (E08 AC5, AC6, AC8, AC9)
- [ ] No semantic judge, overlap planner, custom merge queue, review UI, per-candidate PR, generic host interface, or second acceptance framework is added. (E08 AC10)

## Testing Strategy

- **Unit/fixture:** missing, stale, wrong-fence, superseded, or evidence-mismatched acceptance decisions all block.
- **Fixture/component:** apply multiple non-overlapping accepted candidates and verify deterministic ordered trees/commits, one branch, and one PR.
- **Negative component:** stale mechanical gate, invalid artifact/write-policy identity, unexpected base, conflict, or protected-path change stops before publication.
- **Live integration:** current-head required checks pass through the selected host and existing merge queue/auto-merge; prior-head checks cannot authorize the new head.
- **Fault/live integration:** stop the publisher after branch/PR success but before E04/E05 observation, restart/reclaim, and verify no duplicate authoritative integration.
- **Manual review:** checklist source, dependencies, and created remote resources for one provider path, one campaign PR, no custom CI/merge/review infrastructure, and no semantic/overlap implementation.

title: Define the Trusted Evaluator Generation and Exact Routing
description:
## Context

E08 must route a fixed set of trusted evaluations across local workers and existing code-host CI without allowing candidate/model output to choose evaluators or capabilities. This task establishes the exact action identity used by every later evaluator, evidence, and code-host check path.

The pilot design is fixed: use private concrete configuration and literal labels, not an evaluator platform, manifest language, or dynamic DAG.

## Current State

The repository currently contains `docs/epics.md`, `docs/mvp-outline.md`, Beads metadata, and no source code. This task builds on E01's selected trusted commands/checks, trust roots, labels, limits, workflow revision, and policy; E04's work revision/fence fields; and E07's exact candidate identity (`base_oid`, result tree OID, commit SHA) and distinct evaluator launch-policy type.

Relevant settled design is `docs/mvp-outline.md` §21-§22. Suggested implementation locations from §42 are `pi-campaign/src/domain/evaluation.rs`, `pi-campaign/src/oracle/manifest.rs`, `pi-campaign/src/controller/scheduler.rs`, and `pi-campaign/src/controller/policy.rs`.

## Desired State

A private concrete trusted-action type represents each member of one flat allowlisted required set. Candidate ID, base OID, result tree OID, commit SHA, evaluator ID/version, and policy version remain explicit.

One canonical `evaluator_generation_digest` commits to every execution-affecting trusted field: command or selected-host check identity, evaluator code, hidden inputs, parser, controls, baseline, resource/output limits, workflow revision, policy, and exact literal capability labels. A stable action identity binds the exact candidate subject, explicit evaluator/policy identity, and this digest. Only trusted E01 configuration can construct the action.

Routing succeeds only when the action's literal required labels exactly match the advertised trusted worker/job labels. Unknown IDs, versions, workflow revisions, aliases, case changes, missing labels, and candidate-authored trusted fields fail closed.

## Implementation Guidance

- Keep the type private/internal and concrete. Do not add a trait, registry, plugin loader, evaluator discovery, scoring, public manifest, or evaluator-to-evaluator edges.
- Use the canonical-byte/digest rules already established by E02 rather than inventing another serializer.
- Represent the required evaluations as a flat set. Labels are exact strings or fixed enums from E01; they are not weights or preferences.
- Keep the generation digest compact while committing to all roots. Do not duplicate each root into a wide action-identity hierarchy.
- Models and candidate artifacts may carry an action reference, but trusted code resolves it to the allowlisted action; untrusted input cannot supply commands, roots, labels, limits, or workflow revisions.
- Treat any unknown serialized version or label as an admission error.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A private concrete action type is constructible only from E01 trusted configuration and E07 exact candidate identity. (E08 AC1, AC2)
- [ ] The action explicitly binds candidate ID/base OID/tree OID/commit SHA, evaluator ID/version, and policy version. (E08 AC2)
- [ ] One canonical evaluator-generation digest commits to command/check identity, evaluator code, hidden inputs, parser, controls, baseline, limits, workflow revision, policy, and literal labels. (E08 AC2)
- [ ] Independently changing any digest input or explicit subject/identity field changes the correct digest/action identity. (E08 AC2)
- [ ] Routing requires literal allowlisted capabilities and rejects aliases, case changes, missing/unknown labels, and unknown evaluator/workflow versions. (E08 AC1)
- [ ] Candidate/model input cannot select commands, evaluator roots, workflows, parsers, limits, policy, or capability requirements. (E08 AC1, AC4)
- [ ] The implementation contains no capability scoring, dynamic plugin loading, evaluator DAG, model-authored manifest, or public evaluator framework. (E08 AC1, AC10)

## Testing Strategy

- **Unit:** canonical serialization and round-trip fixtures for every fixed action; a table that mutates each digest field independently; subject/evaluator/policy identity mutation tests.
- **Unit:** exact-label routing table covering matches, missing labels, extras claiming another evaluator, aliases, case changes, and unknown versions.
- **Fixture:** deserialize candidate/model-controlled records containing attempted command, root, workflow, policy, or label overrides and prove trusted construction ignores/rejects them.
- **Manual review:** verify the action is a private concrete type with a flat required set and no plugin/registry/DAG dependencies.

title: Implement concrete launch types and a reap-safe runner
description:
## Context

E07 (`ravel-amn`) must run untrusted generated code without allowing process-lifecycle races to release a writable workspace while candidate descendants still exist. The controlled pilot also needs candidate and evaluator launch contracts that cannot be accidentally substituted.

This task combines the minimum launch-policy types with the first concrete runner. It relies on E01's selected Linux containment/quiescence mechanism and fixed limits; a POSIX process group is used for signaling but is not treated as complete descendant containment.

## Current State

The repository has no Rust code yet. `docs/epics.md` defines E07 criteria 2, 3, 4, and 10. `docs/mvp-outline.md` §19 defines the candidate trust boundary, while §42 names `src/sandbox/policy.rs` and `src/sandbox/process.rs`.

E01 (`ravel-q3w`) is expected to provide the checked-in pilot configuration, selected Linux mechanism, fixed resource/output caps, and authoritative containment/quiescence contract. E02 (`ravel-aq8`) is expected to provide the one Cargo package, pinned runtime/toolchain, and repository test commands. Use those landed outputs directly; do not duplicate them.

## Desired State

The Rust package has distinct concrete `CandidateLaunchSpec` and `EvaluatorLaunchSpec` types beside a concrete candidate runner API. The types carry only fixed pilot inputs, paths, and bounds; they have no secret-bearing field, generic extension map, policy trait, backend selector, or public conversion between trust domains.

A unique runner supervisor owns the child/process-group handles, E01 containment handle, independently bounded stdout/stderr drains, and workspace lease. Natural completion and abnormal termination converge on one awaited sequence: request stop, drain/close pipes, wait for authoritative containment quiescence, reap, then return a reusable workspace disposition. Any unresolved kill, quiescence, or reap result quarantines the workspace. Dropping or aborting the caller requests cancellation but cannot release or reuse the workspace; `Drop` may only best-effort signal or quarantine.

## Implementation Guidance

- Add the narrow concrete types to `src/sandbox/policy.rs` and the runner/supervisor to `src/sandbox/process.rs`, matching the single-crate tree in `docs/mvp-outline.md` §42.
- Use the exact E01 containment API. Create a POSIX process group for immediate signaling, but wait on E01's authority for descendants that escape the group through `setsid` or `setpgid`.
- Keep the workspace lease inside the supervisor until the terminal lifecycle state is known. A caller-facing future or handle must not own the only cleanup authority.
- Bound stdout and stderr separately and drain concurrently. Reaching either cap must not stop draining in a way that leaves the child blocked on a full pipe.
- Keep result modeling minimal: enough internal success/error information to report execution and choose reusable versus quarantined workspace disposition. Do not add a general process-execution framework or a seven-way public outcome taxonomy.
- Use ordinary concrete signatures and constructor tests to prove launch-type separation. Do not add compile-fail scaffolding.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `CandidateLaunchSpec` and `EvaluatorLaunchSpec` are distinct concrete Rust types with no public conversion or generic launcher that makes them interchangeable. (E07 AC3)
- [ ] The candidate spec contains no field for daemon/code-host credentials, hidden evaluator inputs, shared writable caches, unrestricted network policy, or arbitrary extensions. (E07 AC2, AC3)
- [ ] The runner creates/owns a process group for signaling and uses E01's containment/quiescence authority to account for the complete candidate process tree. (E07 AC4)
- [ ] Stdout and stderr have independent fixed caps and cannot cause unbounded allocation or blocked-pipe deadlock. (E07 AC4)
- [ ] A reusable workspace result is impossible until pipes are closed, authoritative quiescence is confirmed, and all candidate processes are reaped. (E07 AC4, AC10)
- [ ] Caller cancellation, future drop, or task abort retains cleanup authority in the supervisor; unresolved termination produces quarantine, never cleanup/reuse. (E07 AC4, AC10)
- [ ] No custom sandbox runtime, backend trait/registry, policy language, or standalone filesystem-plan abstraction is introduced. (E07 AC2)

## Testing Strategy

- **Unit:** constructor tests reject missing/zero E01 bounds and trust-domain-crossing paths; ordinary type-specific API tests exercise candidate and evaluator constructors without compile-fail machinery.
- **Real-process integration:** cover natural exit, timeout, explicit cancellation, simultaneous stdout/stderr pressure, a descendant retaining pipe/workspace descriptors, and a daemonized grandchild that calls `setsid`/`setpgid` and ignores ordinary termination.
- **Lifecycle fault tests:** instrument each lifecycle await and abort the caller at each point. Assert the supervisor still kills, waits, reaps, and only then releases, or quarantines on injected kill/quiescence/reap failure.
- **Manual review:** trace every path that can return or drop a run handle and confirm none can manufacture a reusable workspace token before terminal quiescence.

## Design Gate

title: Materialize and preflight the exact trusted Git base
description:
## Context

E07 (`ravel-amn`) requires candidate generation and later delta verification to start from one exact immutable Git base. Materialization must not expose writable daemon Git metadata or allow ambient Git configuration, replacement refs, attributes, or filters to change bytes or execute helpers.

This task creates the trusted source snapshot and compact base inventory used by isolation, delta validation, and candidate construction.

## Current State

The repository has no implementation code. `docs/epics.md` E07 criteria 1, 6, and 7 require an exact base, fail-closed preflight, and trusted Git construction. `docs/mvp-outline.md` §19 forbids writable `.git`, §20 starts construction from the exact base tree, and §42 names `src/git/repository.rs` and `src/sandbox/filesystem.rs`.

E01 (`ravel-q3w`) is expected to provide the allowed pilot repository and its preflight/path contract. It currently does not state the exact path-component grammar, invalid-UTF-8 rule, Unicode normalization form/version, or case/normalization collision-key algorithm. This task is blocked until one exact checked-in E01 contract exists; do not invent a local canonicalizer.

## Desired State

Trusted code accepts one full exact base commit OID, rejects symbolic/abbreviated/moving references, and materializes its tree with raw Git plumbing under a scrubbed environment. The candidate-visible source has no `.git` directory or other writable daemon repository state.

Each emitted regular file is byte-for-byte verified against its Git blob OID. Unsupported base modes/shapes fail before candidate launch. The retained inventory is minimal: raw path, supported mode, blob OID, base tree OID, and base commit OID; it does not retain a duplicate copy of every base file.

## Implementation Guidance

- Implement trusted repository access in `src/git/repository.rs` and snapshot placement/read-only handoff in `src/sandbox/filesystem.rs`, following `docs/mvp-outline.md` §42.
- Invoke the selected absolute Git binary with replacement objects disabled, system/global config disabled, isolated `HOME` and XDG config, and credential/helper environment removed. Preserve only repository-local settings required to read its actual object format.
- Use NUL-delimited raw tree enumeration (`ls-tree -z` or equivalent) and raw blob streaming (`cat-file`). Do not use checkout, archive, worktree filters, smudge/clean, `export-ignore`, or `export-subst` paths.
- Verify materialized bytes by hashing each emitted file as a raw Git blob without a path argument and comparing the listed OID. Verify executable mode separately.
- Preflight symlinks, gitlinks/submodules, unsupported modes, LFS pointers, nested repository markers, and collisions under the exact E01 path/collision contract.
- Preserve accepted raw path bytes; collision processing detects ambiguity but never rewrites names.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Only one full exact commit OID is accepted; symbolic, abbreviated, ambiguous, missing, or moving references fail before materialization. (E07 AC7)
- [ ] Raw tree/blob plumbing runs under a scrubbed Git environment with replacement-object behavior disabled. (E07 AC6, AC7)
- [ ] Repository-controlled attributes, filters, export directives, aliases, and ambient global/system configuration cannot transform emitted bytes or execute helpers. (E07 AC6, AC7)
- [ ] Every emitted regular file and executable mode matches the base tree entry and blob OID. (E07 AC7)
- [ ] Symlinks, gitlinks/submodules, LFS pointers, nested repository markers, unsupported modes, and E01-defined case/normalization ambiguity fail before candidate launch. (E07 AC6)
- [ ] Candidate-visible source contains no writable `.git` or daemon repository metadata. (E07 AC1)
- [ ] The base inventory stores only path, mode, blob OID, base tree OID, and base commit OID; base file contents are not duplicated. (E07 AC7)

## Testing Strategy

- **Fixture:** build real repositories with ordinary files plus separate fixtures for symlink, gitlink/submodule, LFS pointer, nested `.git`, unsupported mode, and every E01 collision golden vector.
- **Hostile Git fixture:** configure replacement refs, global/system-like config, repository filters/aliases, `.gitattributes`, `export-ignore`, and `export-subst`; assert raw materialization emits the original blob bytes and never runs the helper.
- **Identity fixture:** mutate a branch/ref after exact OID admission and prove the snapshot still matches the pinned commit/tree.
- **Manual review:** inspect every Git invocation for scrubbed environment use, raw/NUL-delimited output parsing, and absence of candidate paths in option positions.

## Design Gate

title: Enforce candidate isolation with the selected Linux mechanism
description:
## Context

E07 (`ravel-amn`) needs one concrete enforcement point for the candidate trust boundary. Generated code may read the exact source/task inputs and write only private attempt-local areas; it must not inherit trusted files, credentials, sockets, Git authority, caches, evaluator material, network access, or unbounded resources.

This task integrates the concrete launch spec and reap-safe runner with the existing Linux isolation mechanism selected by E01. It does not build another sandbox runtime.

## Current State

The repository has no implementation code. Step 1 will provide concrete launch types and a supervisor that retains cleanup authority through authoritative descendant quiescence. Step 2 will provide the exact read-only source snapshot without writable Git metadata.

`docs/epics.md` E07 criteria 1-4 and 10 define the isolation/lifecycle contract. `docs/mvp-outline.md` §19 lists candidate inputs and forbidden surfaces; §42 names `src/sandbox/policy.rs`, `src/sandbox/filesystem.rs`, and `src/sandbox/process.rs`. E01 (`ravel-q3w`) must supply the selected mechanism, fixed mounts/limits, and any descriptors the mechanism requires across exec.

## Desired State

The sole candidate launcher directly builds E01's fixed invocation from `CandidateLaunchSpec`. Source, task inputs, and prefetched dependencies are read-only. Overlay, build, and temporary directories are private to one attempt. Daemon/code-host credentials, evaluator inputs, writable Git metadata, shared writable caches, and network access are absent.

Before candidate exec, every file descriptor is closed except stdin/stdout/stderr and descriptors explicitly required by the selected mechanism. CPU, memory, process, wall-time, filesystem, and output limits fail closed if unavailable. Workspace cleanup/reuse is allowed only after Step 1 returns its reusable disposition; otherwise the workspace remains quarantined.

## Implementation Guidance

- Extend only `src/sandbox/policy.rs`, `src/sandbox/filesystem.rs`, and `src/sandbox/process.rs` as suggested by `docs/mvp-outline.md` §42.
- Construct fixed read-only and private-writable binds directly from E01 config. Do not add a filesystem-plan type, backend trait, registry, adapter, or evaluator launcher.
- Start from an allowlisted environment. Do not forward ambient process environment and then redact it.
- Close the inherited FD table before exec. Keep an explicit small allowlist for stdio and exact E01 control descriptors; do not assume a network namespace neutralizes already-connected or listening sockets.
- Apply both selected-mechanism limits and Step 1 output caps. Missing isolation/limit support is a launch failure, not a permissive fallback.
- Preserve the workspace until the runner proves quiescence/reap. Cleanup code must require the unforgeable reusable disposition rather than a boolean success flag.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Source/task inputs and prefetched dependencies are read-only; overlay/build/temp are private and writable only for one attempt. (E07 AC1, AC2)
- [ ] Candidate execution receives no daemon/code-host credentials, hidden evaluator material, writable daemon Git metadata, or shared writable caches. (E07 AC1)
- [ ] Candidate execution has no network access and cannot use an inherited connected/listening network or Unix-domain socket. (E07 AC1)
- [ ] Every non-required inherited FD is closed before candidate exec; the allowlist contains only stdio and exact selected-mechanism controls. (E07 AC1)
- [ ] Fixed CPU, memory, process, wall-time, filesystem, and output limits are enforced with fail-closed launch behavior. (E07 AC2)
- [ ] The launcher accepts only `CandidateLaunchSpec`; evaluator execution is not added. (E07 AC3)
- [ ] Workspace cleanup/reuse requires Step 1's reusable disposition and therefore cannot precede authoritative descendant quiescence/reap. (E07 AC4, AC10)
- [ ] Exactly one selected Linux integration exists; no custom runtime, pluggable backend, filesystem-plan abstraction, or shared writable cache is introduced. (E07 AC2)

## Testing Strategy

- **Live integration:** from inside the selected sandbox, probe environment variables, conventional credential paths, evaluator paths, source/Git metadata writes, shared cache writes, network creation/connect, and writes outside overlay/build/temp; all forbidden operations must be absent or denied.
- **FD probes:** inherit a regular credential-like file, socketpair, host Unix socket, pre-opened connected TCP/UDP socket, and listening socket in the parent. Inspect `/proc/self/fd` in the candidate and attempt to use each capability; none may survive unless explicitly allowlisted by E01.
- **Resource integration:** exhaust CPU, memory, process count, wall time, filesystem space, stdout, and stderr independently; each case must terminate through Step 1 and prove reap-before-cleanup.
- **Fail-closed checks:** make each required mechanism feature/limit unavailable in turn and assert launch refusal rather than fallback.
- **Manual review:** compare the final invocation and descriptor allowlist to the exact landed E01 configuration.

title: Validate and digest the narrow filesystem delta
description:
## Context

E07 (`ravel-amn`) treats the post-generation filesystem delta as a security boundary. Trusted code must inspect the real workspace, accept only the narrow pilot shape inside explicit write scopes/caps, and reject ambiguity before any Git candidate or durable record is created.

This task returns the sorted validated delta as an in-memory construction input. Candidate identity is bound directly to Git identities — base OID, result tree OID, candidate commit OID — plus the bundle artifact digest (Steps 5–6); there is no separate serialized delta stream or delta digest.

## Current State

The repository has no implementation code. Step 2 will provide the exact base commit/tree inventory as raw path, supported mode, and blob OID. Step 3 will provide the private post-run workspace. `docs/epics.md` E07 criteria 5 and 6 enumerate supported and prohibited shapes; `docs/mvp-outline.md` §19.1 defines post-generation validation and §42 names `src/git/delta.rs` and `src/git/repository.rs` (§20's separate delta digest is superseded by direct Git-identity binding).

E01 (`ravel-q3w`) must provide one exact path-component predicate and collision-key algorithm, including component grammar, invalid-UTF-8 behavior, Unicode normalization form/version, case handling, and golden vectors. Until it does, this task is blocked; do not invent a general canonicalizer.

## Desired State

Trusted validation walks without following links, compares the actual workspace to the base inventory, and returns sorted accepted entries for regular-file add/change/delete and allowed `100644`/`100755` transitions. Accepted entries carry exact bytes only for added/changed files. Directories are structural parents implied by accepted files; standalone empty-directory changes are rejected because Git cannot preserve them without a sentinel.

All E01 write scopes and count/size caps are checked before Git object creation or candidate publication. Every unsupported shape fails through one bounded error carrying a path and reason category. The validator returns the sorted accepted entries (sorted by unsigned raw path bytes; duplicate paths invalid; modes numeric Git modes, pilot permits only `100644` and `100755`) as an in-memory construction input only. Verification on both producer and receiving hosts compares the raw base/result-tree diff — paths, modes, blob identities — against the accepted delta and declared write scopes; no bespoke binary serialization or standalone delta digest exists.

## Implementation Guidance

- Implement the validator in `src/git/delta.rs`; reuse base access and scrubbed raw Git blob hashing from `src/git/repository.rs`.
- Walk by file descriptor or an equivalent no-follow pattern supported by the selected pilot. Do not trust candidate Git metadata, manifests, change reports, or directory enumeration order.
- Detect hard-link aliases using inode/link metadata under the pilot filesystem contract. Reject symlinks, sockets, FIFOs, devices, nested repositories, gitlinks/submodules, LFS pointers, unsupported modes/transitions, out-of-scope paths, and E01-defined path ambiguity.
- Enforce per-file bytes, total changed bytes, changed-file count, directory/count, and write-scope bounds before writing Git objects.
- Preserve raw path bytes in the accepted delta; do not add a digest framework or a bespoke serialization format.
- Return one bounded unsupported-delta error with path plus stable reason category. Do not include file contents or create a distinct public error type for every case.
- Additions and deletions are independent records. Do not infer renames or rewrite names.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Regular-file additions, content changes, deletions, and allowed `100644`/`100755` changes pass only inside E01 write scopes and all caps. (E07 AC5)
- [ ] Directories are accepted only as parents implied by accepted files; empty-directory-only changes fail closed. (E07 AC5, AC6)
- [ ] Symlinks, hard links, special files, nested repositories, submodules/gitlinks, LFS pointers, unsupported modes/transitions, out-of-scope paths, and E01-defined case/normalization/invalid-byte ambiguity fail before Git construction/publication. (E07 AC6)
- [ ] Exact-at-cap inputs pass and over-cap inputs fail for every configured count/size boundary. (E07 AC5, AC6)
- [ ] The accepted delta is sorted by raw path bytes, retains exact accepted bytes/modes, and never trusts a candidate-authored report. (E07 AC5, AC7)
- [ ] No bespoke delta serialization or standalone delta digest exists; the accepted delta is an in-memory construction input with duplicate paths rejected, and candidate identity binds to base OID, result tree OID, candidate commit OID, and bundle digest. (E07 AC7)
- [ ] Enumeration order does not change the accepted sorted delta; fixture vectors pin the exact sorted entry list (operations, raw paths, modes, algorithm-tagged blob identities). (E07 AC7, AC8)
- [ ] Rejection returns one bounded path/reason-category error and leaves no Git candidate object or published record. (E07 AC6)

## Testing Strategy

- **Positive fixture table:** unchanged tree; add/change/delete; content-only, mode-only, and content-plus-mode changes; nested parent directories implied by accepted files.
- **Boundary fixture table:** exact/over per-file bytes, total bytes, file count, directory/count, root/nested/sibling write scopes.
- **Negative fixture table:** empty directory, symlink, hard-link alias, FIFO, socket, device, nested `.git`, submodule/gitlink, LFS pointer, unsupported mode, traversal/out-of-scope path, and every E01 collision golden vector.
- **Delta unit tests:** fixture vectors for add/modify/delete, mode-only change, SHA-1/SHA-256 blob identity kinds, raw path bytes, duplicate rejection, and shuffled enumeration yielding an identical sorted result.
- **Integration:** ensure rejected validation never invokes candidate construction or E02 publication; accepted changed bytes are read once and passed unchanged.
- **Manual review:** compare the path predicate/collision vectors to the landed E01 contract and the accepted-entry shape to the layout above.

## Design Gate

title: Construct the immutable Git candidate from validated bytes
description:
## Context

E07 (`ravel-amn`) gives Git authority only to trusted code. Candidate construction must apply the exact validated bytes to the exact base, tolerate legal adversarial filenames without command/record injection, and create fresh immutable identities for repairs.

This task creates the Git commit and internal constructed-candidate value. Durable candidate publication waits for the transferable artifact in the next task.

## Current State

The repository has no implementation code. Step 2 will provide scrubbed trusted Git access and the exact base. Step 4 will provide sorted validated entries and exact accepted bytes/modes. `docs/mvp-outline.md` §20 requires trusted tree/commit construction and records base/result identities; §42 names `src/git/candidate.rs`, `src/git/repository.rs`, and `src/domain/attempt.rs`.

E02 (`ravel-aq8`) is expected to provide canonical identity/record primitives in the one Rust package. This task uses those concrete primitives without adding an identity framework.

## Desired State

A trusted constructor accepts only an exact base OID, the validated delta, a fresh producer attempt identity, and a fresh candidate identity. It writes accepted blobs through stdin, updates a private index with NUL-delimited records, writes the result tree and immutable commit, and verifies the final tree entry-for-entry against base plus delta.

Candidate-controlled paths never appear in command-line option positions or line-delimited protocols. The constructor returns an internal value containing candidate ID, producer attempt, base OID, result tree OID, and candidate commit OID. It does not publish the immutable candidate record before the bundle exists.

## Implementation Guidance

- Implement construction in `src/git/candidate.rs`, reuse the scrubbed Git invocation from `src/git/repository.rs`, and use attempt/candidate identities from `src/domain/attempt.rs` or the landed E02 domain location.
- Use a private trusted object/index context. Seed the index from the exact base, stream each added/changed file to `git hash-object -w --stdin`, apply add/modify/delete records with `git update-index --index-info -z` (or an equally byte-safe NUL protocol), then run `write-tree` and `commit-tree`.
- Never run broad `git add`, read the workspace after validation, interpolate a candidate path into argv, or encode paths in newline/tab-delimited records without NUL framing.
- Verify the result tree by raw NUL-delimited enumeration. Independently derive the base/result-tree diff (operations, paths, modes, blob identities) from the constructed tree and require it to equal the Step 4 accepted delta before returning.
- Treat leading dashes, tabs, and newlines as data when E01 permits them. If E01's exact grammar rejects a name, rejection belongs to Step 4.
- Keep repair behavior narrow: caller supplies fresh attempt and candidate IDs. No rebase, rename detector, generic patch engine, or mutation of prior evidence.
- Return an internal constructed value only. The immutable durable candidate record is published in Step 6 after artifact upload/verification.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Construction accepts only the exact base, validated delta, fresh attempt identity, and fresh candidate identity; it does not rescan the untrusted workspace. (E07 AC7, AC9)
- [ ] Only validated bytes and `100644`/`100755` modes are written into the result tree. (E07 AC7)
- [ ] Candidate paths never occupy argv/option positions or line-delimited records; the Git index update is byte-safe and NUL-delimited. (E07 AC6, AC7)
- [ ] Leading-dash, tab, and newline filenames are either handled as data or rejected earlier by the exact E01 grammar, never interpreted as options/extra records. (E07 AC6, AC7)
- [ ] The final tree matches base plus validated delta entry-for-entry, with no omitted or extra path. (E07 AC7)
- [ ] Base OID, result tree OID, candidate commit OID, producer attempt ID, and fresh candidate ID are returned in the internal constructed value. (E07 AC7, AC9)
- [ ] A post-validation extra workspace file cannot enter the tree. (E07 AC7)
- [ ] Two repairs with identical bytes have distinct attempt/candidate identities and do not mutate the first candidate. (E07 AC9)
- [ ] No rebase or rename-detection behavior is implemented. (E07 AC9)

## Testing Strategy

- **Real-Git fixture:** construct add/change/delete and mode-change candidates, enumerate the commit/tree independently, and compare every path, mode, byte, and OID to base plus validated delta.
- **Adversarial-name fixture:** cover leading dash, tab, newline, spaces, and non-ASCII/raw bytes allowed by E01; prove no option or record injection.
- **TOCTOU fixture:** add/modify an unvalidated workspace path after validation and prove it cannot affect the candidate.
- **Identity fixture:** vary base, bytes, and mode one at a time; assert the expected tree/commit/delta identity changes or mismatch rejection. Run two identical-content repairs and assert fresh attempt/candidate IDs with unchanged prior data.
- **Manual review:** inspect every Git command and stdin protocol, then confirm no code path performs broad workspace staging or durable publication.

## Design Gate

title: Publish the Git bundle and verify cross-host reconstruction
description:
## Context

E07 (`ravel-amn`) is complete only when the exact candidate can move to another machine and be independently verified. The durable candidate record must bind one candidate to one content-addressed bundle; publication failure or an ambiguous retry must never expose an eligible record without its transferable artifact or require record mutation.

This task owns bundle creation, E02 artifact publication, immutable candidate-record ordering, and the one required cross-host reconstruction proof.

## Current State

The repository has no implementation code. Step 5 will return an internal constructed candidate with candidate/attempt/base/tree/delta/commit identities but no durable candidate record. `docs/mvp-outline.md` §12 defines artifact metadata (`digest`, `size`, `media type`, `producer attempt`, `creation time`, optional retention), §20 requires a Git bundle/patch artifact and immutable candidate records, and §42 names `src/git/bundle.rs`, `src/git/candidate.rs`, `src/git/repository.rs`, and `src/storage/artifacts.rs`.

E02 (`ravel-aq8`) must provide the direct S3 immutable artifact path, full-byte SHA-256 and size verification, canonical immutable-record/event publication, and ambiguous-operation reconciliation. Reuse those concrete APIs; do not add another storage or evidence workflow.

## Desired State

Trusted code creates a bounded Git bundle, computes its SHA-256/size/media type, and uploads/verifies it through E02 before publishing candidate eligibility. One immutable candidate record binds candidate ID, producer attempt, base OID, result tree OID, candidate commit OID, and artifact reference `{digest, size, media_type}`.

Ambiguous artifact upload is reconciled through E02's immutable-key byte/digest rules. Candidate-record publication retries use the same identity and canonical bytes. A definite upload failure publishes no candidate record.

A different selected Linux host fetches by digest, verifies full bytes and size, imports into a fresh repository containing the exact trusted base, verifies commit/tree identities, and independently derives the raw base/result-tree diff — operations, paths, modes, blob identities — comparing it against the record's identities and declared write scopes. It does not trust the generator report.

## Implementation Guidance

- Add bundle/reconstruction logic in `src/git/bundle.rs`; assemble the final immutable record in `src/git/candidate.rs`; reuse `src/git/repository.rs` and E02's `src/storage/artifacts.rs` implementation.
- Use the fixed bounded Git bundle shape for the candidate commit with the exact base prerequisite. Use media type `application/x-git-bundle` unless E02 has already pinned a more specific constant.
- Publication order is strict: create bundle -> compute SHA-256/size -> immutable upload -> fetch/verify or reconcile -> publish canonical candidate record. No candidate record/eligibility exists before verified artifact availability.
- On upload ambiguity, accept an existing immutable key only after E02 full-byte SHA-256 and size verification. On candidate-record ambiguity, use E02's operation/chain reconciliation and retry only identical bytes.
- Reconstruction must use a fresh trusted repository/cache, require the exact base, verify artifact digest/size before Git consumes it, import the selected commit, and compare base/commit/tree identities plus the re-derived diff.
- Re-derive the raw base/result-tree diff (operation, length-safe raw path, old/new numeric modes, algorithm-tagged old/new blob OIDs) from the trusted base and imported result trees; compare paths, modes, blob identities, and declared write scopes exactly.
- Do not scan harmless extra unreachable objects in the already size-bounded, digest-verified trusted bundle. Do not publish second-host verification as another artifact/event.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The bundle is immutable, bounded, content-addressed by SHA-256, and carries E02 artifact metadata including size, media type, producer attempt, and creation time. (E07 AC7)
- [ ] The immutable candidate record contains candidate ID, producer attempt, base OID, result tree OID, candidate commit OID, and artifact `{digest, size, media_type}`. (E07 AC7, AC9)
- [ ] Artifact upload/verification completes before candidate-record publication; definite failure exposes no eligible candidate. (E07 AC7)
- [ ] Ambiguous upload/publication retries reconcile through E02 and reuse identical identity/bytes; no record is mutated. (E07 AC7, AC9)
- [ ] A fresh repository on a different selected host reconstructs the candidate from the exact base plus fetched bundle. (E07 AC8)
- [ ] The receiving host verifies artifact digest/size before use and independently recomputes commit and tree identities and the raw base/result-tree diff (including write-scope compliance) without trusting the generator report. (E07 AC8)
- [ ] Corrupted/substituted bundle, wrong/missing base, malformed import, or any candidate-record identity mismatch fails closed. (E07 AC8)
- [ ] The implementation uses only E02's concrete direct-S3 artifact/record path; no object-store abstraction, multipart path, unreachable-object scanner, or verification-evidence workflow is added. (E07 AC2, AC7, AC8)

## Testing Strategy

- **Unit:** canonical candidate-record tests pin artifact-reference fields and prove retries serialize identical bytes/identity.
- **Fixture integration:** round-trip bundles through a fresh repository; corrupt or substitute bundle bytes, size, digest, base, commit, tree, and artifact metadata one at a time and assert fail-closed behavior.
- **Publication fault integration:** inject definite and ambiguous upload/record outcomes. Assert no record precedes the artifact, existing keys require full-byte verification, and retries never mutate a candidate.
- **Live integration:** generate/upload one supported candidate on one selected Linux host, then fetch into a clean repository/cache on a second host and independently verify every identity. Run one receiving-path fail-closed mismatch case; keep exhaustive corruptions in local fixtures.
- **Manual review:** verify publication ordering, E02 reconciliation reuse, absence of a second evidence artifact/event, and absence of a generic storage interface.

## Design Gate

title: Extend the Versioned Campaign Head as the Sole Authority Record
description:
## Context

E05 requires controller ownership and authoritative event publication to share one Amazon S3 campaign-head CAS domain. This task establishes the record that later acquisition, renewal, takeover, readiness, and event-commit work will use.

The pilot must keep the durable design narrow: one versioned head, one head key, and no independent controller record.

## Current State

The repository currently contains `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/epics.md`, `docs/mvp-outline.md`, and Beads metadata; it has no Rust source yet. `docs/epics.md` E05 AC1 and `docs/mvp-outline.md` §§6–7 define the combined authority/tail record. This task starts after E02 has created the single `pi-campaign` package/node binary, the versioned event/head envelope, canonical encoding, opaque ETags, and the one campaign-head key. E01's private pilot configuration remains fixed and gains no schema or migration machinery here.

## Desired State

E02 (ravel-aq8.2) already froze the complete v1 head superset: explicit `Unowned | Owned { owner, instance, lease_until, controller_fence }`, authoritative event-tail sequence/digest/key, and the operation identity of the head mutation that produced it. This task adds no fields and changes no v1 bytes. It implements validation and authority-state transitions over those frozen fields: candidate replacements fail closed if they regress fence or tail or contain an invalid field combination.

There is no `controller.json`, second authoritative key, or duplicate envelope framework. The head operation ID is not implicitly reused as the next event commit's operation ID.

## Implementation Guidance

- Build on the frozen types in `pi-campaign/src/sync/head.rs` without modifying the v1 byte contract; expose controller-facing validated values through `pi-campaign/src/distributed/controller.rs` only as needed.
- Reuse E02's version tag, canonical encoding/decoding, unknown-version failure, opaque ETag type, and single head-key constant.
- Model only the owned and unowned states required by E05. Reject malformed partial authority, invalid tail metadata, lower replacement fences, and tail regression.
- Keep controller authority and event tail in the same serialized object and replacement validation path.
- Do not add a generic schema layer, migration framework, controller record, or source-layout test that is more brittle than the behavior it protects.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Controller validation covers the frozen head fields — owner/instance, lease, monotonic fence, event-tail sequence/digest/key, and operation identity — in one validated object, with no change to the E02 v1 byte contract and no added fields. (E05 AC1)
- [ ] The initial/unowned and owned states round-trip through E02's canonical envelope and invalid field combinations fail closed. (E05 AC1)
- [ ] Candidate head replacement rejects a lower controller fence and a regressing or internally inconsistent event tail. (E05 AC3 support)
- [ ] The implementation reuses one E02 campaign-head key and introduces no separately authoritative controller object or CAS path. (E05 AC1–AC2)
- [ ] Unknown envelope versions continue to fail before conversion to controller domain values. (E05 AC1)
- [ ] No schema/migration framework or portable storage abstraction is added.

## Testing Strategy

- **Unit:** round-trip focused owned/unowned values; reject malformed authority/tail combinations and fence/tail regression.
- **Fixture:** reuse E02's frozen unowned/owned head fixtures unchanged; do not duplicate E02's full malformed-envelope matrix.
- **Live integration:** none in this task; E02 owns generic live head encoding/CAS coverage and E05's cross-host proof is separately gated.
- **Manual review:** confirm one head-key constant, one authoritative head representation, and no `controller.json` or parallel CAS domain.
