title: Serialize Head Mutations and Manage Opaque Controller Authority
description:
## Context

E05 requires acquisition, renewal, takeover, and publication to replace the same observed campaign head. Within one controller process, those operations must not concurrently consume the same ETag-bound authority or allow an ambiguous renewal to leave stale authority usable.

This task creates the minimum authority state machine and one local serialization point. S3 CAS remains the cross-host arbiter; no distributed lock or generic lease framework is introduced.

## Current State

The repository currently has no source code. `docs/mvp-outline.md` §7 defines the controller lease/fence role, and §6 defines head CAS plus operation-ID reconciliation. Step 1 supplies the combined validated campaign head. E02 supplies direct AWS SDK conditional writes, opaque ETags, typed ambiguous outcomes, and current-head/retained-chain reconciliation. E01 supplies the fixed pilot lease policy; this task does not add configuration knobs.

## Desired State

One controller-head mutation component per process owns the current validated head snapshot plus observed ETag and serializes acquisition, renewal, takeover, publication requests, and their reconciliation. A private, non-forgeable authority value wraps exactly that snapshot and ETag. Acquisition/takeover advances the fence; renewal preserves fence and tail; every successful or positively reconciled mutation refreshes authority.

An ambiguous renewal enters `UNCERTAIN`. The holder may reconcile but cannot publish or make policy decisions. It resumes only after acknowledged or positively reconciled renewal. At the previously pinned lease-expiry-minus-margin deadline it enters `STOPPED`, drops authority, and must reacquire from a fresh head.

## Implementation Guidance

- Implement the mutation owner in `pi-campaign/src/distributed/controller.rs`; keep fence rules in `pi-campaign/src/distributed/fencing.rs`, head conversion/validation in `pi-campaign/src/sync/head.rs`, and direct SDK operations in `pi-campaign/src/storage/s3.rs`.
- Represent authority as one private value containing the validated head snapshot and opaque observed ETag. Read owner/fence/operation/tail/version from the snapshot rather than duplicating fields.
- Route every local campaign-head mutation through one serial owner/loop so renewal and publication cannot race on the same ETag.
- Advance the controller fence only on acquisition or expired-lease takeover. Renewal must preserve fence and tail exactly.
- Pin the safe local stop deadline from the last positively known lease term. Never extend it on an ambiguous response.
- Reuse E02's ambiguity machinery. Add one representative E05 CAS conflict and the E05 lost-renewal-success path, not another timeout/reset/409/412 matrix.
- Expose no constructor accepting raw owner IDs, fences, or ETags.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Acquisition, renewal, and takeover conditionally replace the same campaign head using the authority's observed opaque ETag. (E05 AC2)
- [ ] One local mutation component serializes renewal, publication requests, takeover handling, and reconciliation and owns the only current authority value. (E05 AC2)
- [ ] The private authority value wraps one validated head snapshot and observed ETag and cannot be forged from raw IDs/fences/ETags by callers. (E05 AC2)
- [ ] Acquisition/takeover advances the monotonic fence; renewal preserves fence and event tail. (E05 AC2–AC3)
- [ ] An ambiguous renewal permits reconciliation only, reaches `STOPPED` at the pinned old-expiry-minus-margin deadline if unresolved, and requires fresh reacquisition after stopping. (E05 AC2, AC8)
- [ ] A lost renewal acknowledgement may restore authority only through positive operation-identity reconciliation; a pause beyond expiry cannot revive old authority. (E05 AC2–AC3)
- [ ] No generic lock, lease framework, second controller object, or additional pilot configuration surface is introduced.

## Testing Strategy

- **Unit:** authority state transitions, fence preservation/advance, pinned stop deadline, `UNCERTAIN → STOPPED`, and constructor visibility/compile boundary.
- **Fixture/integration:** race two acquirers/takers; serialize renewal against publication/takeover; inject one CAS conflict and one lost successful renewal response; pause beyond expiry and verify reacquisition is required.
- **Live integration:** deferred to the focused cross-host failover task; generic S3 response permutations remain E02 coverage.
- **Manual review:** verify every local head mutation routes through the single mutation component and no raw-fence/ETag commit API exists.

## Design Gate

title: Commit Events Through the Fenced Campaign-Head CAS
description:
## Context

Controller fencing is effective only if authoritative event publication uses the same ETag-bound campaign head that grants ownership. Each logical event commit also needs its own stable operation identity so a lost success can be found after later head mutations supersede the visible operation ID.

This task implements the sole event-commit boundary. Immutable upload alone is never authoritative; only the fenced head CAS advances history.

## Current State

The repository currently has no source code. `docs/mvp-outline.md` §6 specifies immutable event `N+1`, create-if-absent upload, head `If-Match`, and operation-ID reconciliation; §7 requires every authoritative decision to carry the current controller fence. E02 supplies canonical event bytes, immutable create-if-absent publication, complete retained-chain lookup, and no eager deletion. Steps 1–2 supply the combined head and serialized private authority.

## Desired State

The only authoritative commit API accepts current private authority, an exact readiness witness, and canonical event content. It creates a fresh stable operation ID once per logical event commit, stores it in both event and candidate head, and reuses it only for that commit's retry/reconciliation. The event's parent and writer fence exactly match current authority.

The immutable event is uploaded first, then the same campaign head is replaced with `If-Match` on the authority ETag. CAS revalidates owner, fence, parent, non-regression, and readiness bound to exact `(owner, fence, tail)`. Before readiness, only renewal is allowed. Ambiguous results search current head and the complete retained chain; harmless orphans are retained by recovery.

## Implementation Guidance

- Use `pi-campaign/src/sync/event.rs`, `pi-campaign/src/sync/head.rs`, `pi-campaign/src/distributed/controller.rs`, `pi-campaign/src/storage/s3.rs`, and `pi-campaign/src/recovery/reconcile.rs`.
- Generate the event operation ID before the first upload. Do not copy the operation ID already stored in the authority head.
- Persist identical operation ID and canonical event identity across retries of one logical commit.
- Construct parent sequence/digest/key only from the authority's validated tail. Never accept caller-supplied parent/fence metadata.
- Perform create-if-absent event upload, then head `If-Match` through the serialized mutation owner.
- Revalidate readiness cursor equality with authority owner/fence/tail at the final commit boundary. A boolean `ready` flag is insufficient.
- On ambiguous head response, use E02's current-head and complete retained-parent-chain operation lookup. A chain gap stays unresolved; do not relink or delete uploaded objects.
- Return authority for the resulting head and invalidate readiness until the projection reaches its new tail.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every logical event commit has a fresh stable operation ID distinct from the preceding head mutation and stores it in both event and candidate head. (E05 AC1–AC3)
- [ ] Retries/reconciliation of that logical event reuse the same operation ID and canonical bytes; unrelated commits never reuse it. (E05 AC2–AC3)
- [ ] Event `N+1` carries the exact current parent sequence/digest/key and current controller fence. (E05 AC3)
- [ ] Authoritative publication is create-if-absent event upload followed by `If-Match` replacement of the same campaign head owned by the private authority. (E05 AC2)
- [ ] The CAS boundary rejects commits unless readiness matches exact authority `(owner, fence, tail)`; a direct post-takeover commit is rejected while renewal remains permitted. (E05 AC2, AC4)
- [ ] A fence-`F` commit cannot become authoritative after fence `F+1` wins, even if the old event upload succeeded. (E05 AC3)
- [ ] Lost-success reconciliation finds a committed operation through retained history after later head advancement or takeover; a gap remains unresolved and recovery performs no eager deletion. (E05 AC3, AC9)

## Testing Strategy

- **Unit:** parent/fence/non-regression checks, exact readiness comparison, fresh operation-ID generation, and readiness invalidation after commit.
- **Fixture/integration:** commit two consecutive events and assert distinct IDs; lose the first CAS response, advance/supersede the head, and recover the first ID through chain lookup; delay a fence-`F` commit until `F+1` wins.
- **Live integration:** stale-writer behavior is proven separately on real S3; this task uses E02's protocol harness.
- **Manual review:** confirm there is no other authoritative event-publication entry point and recovery never deletes or relinks orphan events.

## Design Gate

title: Bind Replacement Readiness to the Exact Authority and Tail
description:
## Context

Winning controller authority proves permission to sequence work, not knowledge of current campaign history. A replacement must not make its first authoritative decision until its disposable SQLite projection exactly matches a fresh S3 head.

Readiness must be bound to the same owner, fence, and tail checked by event commit. Renewal-only ETag changes must not livelock a long replay, while tail or authority changes must invalidate the appropriate proof.

## Current State

The repository currently has no source code. `docs/epics.md` E05 AC4 and `docs/mvp-outline.md` §§6–7 require sync before resumed control. E03 supplies complete parent-chain traversal without S3 `LIST`, digest/version/parent validation, transactional projection apply, and a verified `(sequence, tail_digest)` cursor. Steps 2–3 supply private authority and the commit-boundary readiness check.

## Desired State

Acquisition/takeover yields not-ready authority. The controller freshly reads the head, replays through E03, and establishes readiness only when the verified projection cursor matches the exact head tail and the head still names the same owner/fence. The readiness witness is bound to `(owner, fence, tail)` and is consumed/rechecked by event commit.

A renewal-only ETag/lease change with unchanged owner/fence/tail refreshes authority without forcing replay. A same-owner/fence tail advance drops readiness and replays. An owner/fence change drops readiness and authority. Invalid history always fails closed.

## Implementation Guidance

- Use `pi-campaign/src/sync/replay.rs`, `pi-campaign/src/sync/cursor.rs`, `pi-campaign/src/db/projections.rs`, and `pi-campaign/src/distributed/controller.rs`.
- Freshly read the campaign head and traverse exact immutable parents through E03; do not establish readiness from S3 `LIST` or local cache state.
- Bind the readiness value to authority owner, controller fence, and complete tail identity. Keep it private and non-forgeable.
- Compare semantic head fields when the ETag changes:
  - unchanged owner/fence/tail: accept latest authority ETag and retain readiness;
  - unchanged owner/fence with advanced tail: clear readiness and replay to the new tail;
  - changed owner or fence: clear readiness and authority.
- Permit renewal during replay, but let no policy proposal/event commit pass until exact readiness exists.
- Reuse E03's invalid-history fixtures in one parameterized test for gaps, unknown versions, digest/parent mismatch, and conversion failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Acquisition or takeover starts not ready and cannot authorize policy/event commits before exact projection verification. (E05 AC4)
- [ ] Readiness is bound to exact current owner, fence, and event tail and is enforced by the event commit boundary. (E05 AC2, AC4)
- [ ] Replay uses a fresh head and E03's complete parent-chain traversal; projection cursor must exactly equal the fresh tail. (E05 AC4)
- [ ] Gaps, unknown versions, digest/parent failures, conversion failures, and cursor mismatch leave readiness false and preserve E03 atomicity. (E05 AC4)
- [ ] Renewal-only ETag/lease changes with unchanged owner/fence/tail do not force replay or livelock readiness. (E05 AC4)
- [ ] A tail advance forces replay, while owner/fence change invalidates readiness and old authority. (E05 AC3–AC4)
- [ ] A direct event commit immediately after takeover is rejected; renewal remains legal while synchronization runs. (E05 AC2, AC4)

## Testing Strategy

- **Unit:** readiness binding/invalidation for renewal-only, tail-change, and owner/fence-change cases.
- **Fixture:** parameterize E03's existing empty/stale/current and invalid-history fixtures rather than copying their full matrix.
- **Integration:** race head renewal/tail/authority changes between replay and final readiness comparison and assert the correct retain/replay/drop outcome.
- **Live integration:** exact stale-SQLite takeover is repeated in the gated cross-host task; no credentials are required here.
- **Manual review:** confirm no free-standing boolean can bypass the commit-boundary tuple check and no `LIST`-based readiness path exists.

title: Resume Sealed Submissions Through a Pure Policy Function
description:
## Context

E05 must separate deterministic policy from authority while still proving failover makes progress. A replacement controller must rebuild, preserve unexpired E04 claims, process sealed submissions, and sequence resulting transitions without the old host returning.

The minimum product surface is one concrete pure policy function inside the failover/resume path, not a standalone framework or public policy API.

## Current State

The repository currently has no source code. `docs/mvp-outline.md` §7 lists controller decisions and states that the controller emits work rather than executing expensive tasks. E01 supplies fixed private pilot policy/budget values. E03 supplies immutable projected campaign observations. E04 supplies opaque claim authority, same-key `SEALED/SUBMITTED` state, immutable result identity validation, unexpired-claim survival across controller replacement, and request-identity reconciliation. Steps 2–4 supply takeover, fenced event commit, and exact readiness.

## Desired State

One synchronous value-only function consumes concrete immutable projected state plus validated sealed-submission facts and returns a fixed E05 transition enum. It has no S3/provider/database/authority/clock/task capability and cannot reach storage or commit constructors.

After takeover and exact readiness, the controller discovers durable sealed submissions, validates them through E04 intake (which returns validated sealed-submission facts and never commits events itself), preserves unexpired claims, calls the pure function, and commits proposals only through the fenced event API. Authoritative completion commitment lives here and only here: the current ready controller consumes ravel-vsg.5's facts and commits the resulting accepted/completed events solely through ravel-8zo.3's fenced head CAS, deduplicated by stable operation identity. Each accepted valid submission eventually reaches one authoritative terminal transition under available-host/S3 retry assumptions or remains in an explicit durable unresolved state that blocks unsafe retry. No old-host response or machine-departure event is required.

## Implementation Guidance

- Put the concrete pure function and fixed transition enum in `pi-campaign/src/controller/policy.rs`; orchestrate it from `pi-campaign/src/controller/scheduler.rs` and `pi-campaign/src/distributed/controller.rs`.
- Reuse E04 claim/submission types in `pi-campaign/src/distributed/claims.rs` and concrete reconciliation in `pi-campaign/src/recovery/reconcile.rs`.
- Keep the policy entry point synchronous and value-only. Do not accept clients, opaque authority, mutable database handles, clocks, task spawners, closures with effects, or generic capabilities.
- Keep storage and event-commit constructors private to their owning modules so policy cannot bypass the fenced commit path.
- Do not add a policy trait, plugin, DSL, rule engine, generic scheduler, or public orchestration API for one caller.
- Preserve active unexpired E04 claims exactly; controller replacement does not cancel, recreate, or reclaim them.
- Reconcile submission/event outcomes by stable identities. A durable unresolved state must suppress unsafe retry until evidence resolves it.
- Keep submission-boundary crash permutations out of this task; the hermetic fault-matrix task owns them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Controller policy is one synchronous deterministic function over concrete immutable values and returns a fixed transition enum. (E05 AC5)
- [ ] Policy receives no S3/provider/database/authority/task capability and cannot access storage or event-commit constructors through module visibility. (E05 AC5)
- [ ] The replacement cannot call policy until exact readiness and can publish a proposal only through the fenced event commit API. (E05 AC2, AC4–AC5)
- [ ] The replacement discovers and validates E04 sealed submissions and processes them without requiring the former controller to return. (E05 AC6)
- [ ] Authoritative completion commitment happens only in this path: the current ready controller consumes ravel-vsg.5's validated sealed-submission facts and commits accepted/completed events solely through ravel-8zo.3's fenced head CAS, deduplicated by stable operation identity; repeated consumption of one fact records one completion. (E05 AC4–AC6)
- [ ] Unexpired claims remain valid and are neither cancelled nor recreated solely because controller ownership changed. (E05 AC6)
- [ ] Each accepted valid submission reaches one authoritative terminal transition or a durable unresolved state that blocks unsafe retry. (E05 AC6)
- [ ] No machine-departure event, exactly-once remote-effect claim, policy framework, or new public product surface is introduced.

## Testing Strategy

- **Unit:** repeated policy calls over equal inputs return equal transitions; relevant projected facts change the expected transition; irrelevant local/cache/presence noise is absent from the input type.
- **Fixture/integration:** one successful takeover from E03/E04 fixtures preserves an unexpired claim, processes a sealed submission, commits through fenced authority, and makes progress with the old controller absent.
- **Live integration:** full host death and resume are deferred to the gated live task.
- **Manual review:** inspect the policy module dependency/API boundary and verify it cannot import or receive storage, provider, authority, database, or spawn capabilities.

title: Own the Bounded Node Lifecycle and Ordered Shutdown
description:
## Context

E05 requires one node ownership root for every renewal, sync, scheduling, invocation, and publication task and every local admission queue. The same owner must shut the tree down in an order that preserves remote-outcome ambiguity instead of assuming cancellation stopped an S3 or provider operation.

Supervisor ownership and shutdown are one lifecycle contract, so this task implements them together. It does not create a generic executor or effect framework.

## Current State

The repository currently has no source code. `docs/epics.md` E05 AC7–AC8 defines bounded admission, no detached tasks, ordered shutdown, reconciliation, and reaping. E01 supplies fixed pilot limits where already defined; otherwise this task uses named internal constants rather than adding configuration fields. E02/E04 supply operation/request identity reconcilers. Steps 2, 4, and 5 supply authority renewal, readiness/sync, scheduler/submission, invocation ownership points, and publication behavior.

## Desired State

The single node binary has one supervisor that creates and retains every long-lived loop and descendant handle. Every admission queue is bounded and reports full/stopping explicitly. Child failure/panic propagates to the supervisor; no work detaches or survives supervisor return.

Shutdown closes admission, stops new dequeue/dispatch, requests cancellation, collects child outcomes, classifies/reconciles interrupted remote effects with the owning E02/E04 mechanism, then joins or reaps every retained handle. Local cancellation never implies a remote effect stopped.

## Implementation Guidance

- Keep the top-level supervisor in the single node binary. Loop entry points belong in `pi-campaign/src/distributed/controller.rs` and `pi-campaign/src/controller/scheduler.rs`; use `pi-campaign/src/recovery/reconcile.rs` for concrete reconciliation.
- Give renewal, synchronization/readiness, scheduling/submission, invocation, and publication paths explicit bounded queues only where they admit local work. Use named fixed capacities unless an existing E01 pilot field already supplies that exact bound.
- Retain every child handle in the supervisor/owning loop. Nested work returns an outcome record; never discard a handle or spawn detached cleanup/reconciliation.
- Implement shutdown in this order: close admission; stop new dequeue/dispatch; request cancellation; collect outcomes; reconcile unknown remote effects while identities/handles remain available; join/reap all children; return.
- Instantiate this concrete disposition table:

| Work class | Accepted but not dispatched | In-flight effect/cancellation | Required outcome | Reap order |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Renewal | Do not start after close | Abandoned request may have committed; keep pinned old stop deadline and reconcile head operation ID | renewed, known-not-renewed, or unresolved/stopped | reconcile/drop authority, then join renewal child |
| Sync/readiness | Discard queued trigger; fresh head can retrigger after restart | Stop between fetch/apply units; E03 transaction remains atomic | exact cursor, clean cancellation, or invalid history | finish/rollback apply, then join sync child |
| Scheduling/sealed submission | Durable submission remains discoverable; discard local proposal | Stop before publication dispatch; no durable effect yet | explicit stopping/retry-from-durable-input | release permit, then join scheduler child |
| Invocation | Return stopping for undispatched local work | Cancellation of local wait may leave remote work | known success, known failure, or unresolved | record outcome, then join invocation child |
| Event publication | Discard proposal; durable input is rediscoverable | Upload/head CAS may have committed after local cancellation | committed, known-not-committed, or unresolved after operation-ID reconciliation | reconcile while identity/handle is retained, then join publisher child |

- Test semantic lifecycle boundaries here, not every loop × remote-fault permutation. The dedicated fault matrix owns campaign boundary failures.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] One supervisor owns renewal, sync/readiness, scheduling/submission, invocation, publication, and every descendant task handle. (E05 AC7)
- [ ] Every local admission queue has a fixed finite capacity and explicit full/stopping outcomes; no unbounded fallback exists. (E05 AC7)
- [ ] Capacities use existing E01 fields when exact, otherwise named internal constants; no new pilot configuration knobs are added. (E05 AC7)
- [ ] Child completion, error, and panic are visible to the supervisor, and no detached task can renew, schedule, invoke, or publish after supervisor return. (E05 AC7)
- [ ] Shutdown closes admission and prevents new dispatch before requesting cancellation. (E05 AC8)
- [ ] Each queued/in-flight work class follows the disposition table, including permits, outcome record, reconciliation owner, and handle reap order. (E05 AC8)
- [ ] Interrupted remote effects are classified known success, known failure, or unresolved and reconciled by E02/E04 identities where required; cancellation alone is never treated as proof of non-commit. (E05 AC8)
- [ ] All handles are joined or reaped before supervisor return, including after child error/panic or bounded shutdown escalation. (E05 AC7–AC8)
- [ ] No generic executor, effect journal, reconciliation framework, or task plugin API is added.

## Testing Strategy

- **Unit:** queue capacities/full/stopping outcomes, admission state transitions, disposition-table outcomes, and child error/panic propagation.
- **Fixture/integration:** fill each actual admission queue to its cap; assert admission closes first, queued work follows its documented disposition, and every handle is reaped. Simulate one ambiguous event-publication success after local cancellation and reconcile before exit.
- **Concurrency/lifecycle:** wait for supervisor completion and assert no later renewal, sync, scheduling, invocation, or publication activity occurs.
- **Live integration:** queue saturation and shutdown are intentionally not repeated in the live cross-host proof.
- **Manual review:** enumerate every spawn/channel site and confirm an owner, finite capacity, stop behavior, outcome record, and retained handle.

## Design Gate

title: Run the Credential-Free E05 Fault Matrix
description:
## Context

E05 safety and liveness depend on races and ambiguous outcomes that success-path tests cannot prove. The epic explicitly requires lost head-CAS success followed by supersession, stale-controller writes, stale SQLite takeover, submission-processing failure, and restart reconciliation without eager orphan deletion.

This task keeps those deterministic checks credential-free and separate from the slower multi-host S3 proof. It adds no fake production backend.

## Current State

The repository currently has no source code. E02 is expected to provide a concrete S3 protocol/ambiguity harness and retained-chain operation lookup. E03 is expected to provide disposable stale/invalid SQLite fixtures. E04 is expected to provide claim/sealed-submission fixtures and request-identity reconciliation. Steps 1–6 provide combined head authority, serialized mutation, per-event operation IDs, readiness, failover/resume, and owned shutdown. `docs/epics.md` E05 AC9 names the required failures.

## Desired State

Default credential-free CI runs five deterministic, reproducible E05 campaigns using one-shot fault hooks at event upload/head CAS, readiness comparison, sealed-submission processing, and restart. Each run records the fault point and operation identity, proves the required safety/liveness result, and asserts product recovery performs no eager deletion.

Test-created objects are retained through evidence assertions, then the test harness may clean its isolated prefix. Production recovery never performs that cleanup.

## Implementation Guidance

- Exercise `pi-campaign/src/storage/s3.rs`, `pi-campaign/src/distributed/controller.rs`, `pi-campaign/src/sync/replay.rs`, `pi-campaign/src/controller/scheduler.rs`, and `pi-campaign/src/recovery/reconcile.rs`.
- Reuse E02's concrete protocol harness rather than introducing a storage trait/fake backend.
- Reuse E03 stale/invalid history fixtures and E04 claim/submission fixtures; add only E05 composition and fault scheduling.
- Make each fault one-shot and deterministic. Record logical commit operation ID, head owner/fence/tail, fault point, and restart action.
- Required scenarios:
  1. Event head CAS commits, response is lost, a higher-fence takeover supersedes the visible head operation ID, and retained-chain lookup finds the original fresh per-commit ID.
  2. A fence-`F` delayed event upload/CAS arrives after fence `F+1` takeover, cannot advance the head, and any uploaded object remains a harmless orphan.
  3. A replacement starts from stale SQLite, replays/verifies the fresh exact head, and cannot commit before readiness.
  4. Sealed-submission processing fails before upload, after upload/before head CAS, and after head CAS/before local acknowledgement; restart produces one authoritative terminal transition or a durable unresolved blocker.
  5. Restart reconciliation classifies retained operations and performs no eager orphan deletion.
- Do not repeat generic E02 provider-error permutations, Step 6 queue saturation, or live host orchestration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A deterministic lost-success/supersession case finds the original event commit by its fresh operation ID through complete retained history. (E05 AC2–AC3, AC9)
- [ ] A deterministic delayed stale-controller write after higher-fence takeover cannot advance the campaign head. (E05 AC3, AC9)
- [ ] A stale-SQLite takeover cannot make an authoritative decision before exact fresh-head readiness. (E05 AC4, AC9)
- [ ] Failures before upload, after upload/before head CAS, and after head CAS/before local acknowledgement are covered for sealed-submission processing. (E05 AC6, AC9)
- [ ] Recovery yields one authoritative terminal transition per accepted valid submission or a durable unresolved blocker, never an unsafe duplicate. (E05 AC6)
- [ ] Restart reconciliation performs no eager event/orphan deletion and leaves a chain gap unresolved. (E05 AC8–AC9)
- [ ] All fault campaigns run without repository credentials in default CI and record enough identity/state to reproduce failures.
- [ ] Test-harness cleanup occurs only after no-eager-deletion/evidence assertions and is not reachable from product recovery code.

## Testing Strategy

- **Unit:** one-shot fault-hook arming/firing and captured operation/fault metadata.
- **Fixture/integration:** run all five required scenarios with E02/E03/E04 fixtures, including the three submission-processing boundaries as one parameterized campaign.
- **Repeatability:** rerun scenarios under deterministic schedules and assert identical terminal classification/head history.
- **Live integration:** none in this task; real S3 cross-host behavior is a separately gated task.
- **Manual review:** confirm every E05 AC9 scenario is mapped, product recovery has no delete call, and cleanup is isolated to test infrastructure after evidence capture.

## Design Gate

title: Prove Live Cross-Host Failover and Zombie Rejection
description:
## Context

E05 must prove real multi-host controller failover on the selected Amazon S3 boundary. A single scenario cannot both kill the old controller and later make that same process issue a delayed zombie write, so progress and zombie rejection require separate live runs.

This task is credentialed and opt-in. It stays focused on takeover, continued work, and stale-writer rejection; bounded queues and shutdown are already proven hermetically.

## Current State

The repository currently has no source code. E01 is expected to select the pilot S3 environment and fixed identity/lease settings. E02 is expected to provide the pinned AWS SDK live harness and direct conditional-write boundary. E03/E04 provide rebuild, claims, and sealed submissions. Steps 1–7 provide the completed E05 implementation and deterministic fault harness. `docs/mvp-outline.md` §7 defines host-independent controller failover and §6 defines authoritative head publication.

## Desired State

A separately gated live harness runs against the selected general-purpose S3 bucket from at least two independent hosts or process environments. One run kills controller A and proves controller C takes over, rebuilds, processes a sealed submission, preserves an unexpired claim, and continues work without A. A second run pauses A past its safe term, lets C take over, resumes A, and proves A's delayed stale write is rejected.

Each run captures inspectable authority/history/projection/claim evidence. Recovery performs no eager deletion. After evidence capture, the harness cleans only its isolated test prefix.

## Implementation Guidance

- Exercise the direct SDK boundary in `pi-campaign/src/storage/s3.rs` plus `pi-campaign/src/distributed/controller.rs`, `pi-campaign/src/sync/replay.rs`, `pi-campaign/src/controller/scheduler.rs`, and `pi-campaign/src/recovery/reconcile.rs`.
- Reuse E02's credentialed live setup and the completed hermetic fault harness; do not add a portable object-store layer.
- Use unique isolated campaign/test prefixes and independently configured host/process identities.
- Run two scenarios:
  1. **Kill/failover/progress:** A owns the campaign; a worker holds an unexpired E04 claim and publishes a sealed submission; kill A; C acquires a higher fence, rebuilds/verifies its exact projection, processes the submission, and continues authoritative work.
  2. **Pause/takeover/zombie rejection:** pause A before a prepared write, let its safe local term and lease expire, let C acquire a higher fence, resume A, release the delayed write, and assert S3 rejects A's head CAS.
- Capture head ETags, owners, fences, tails, per-event operation IDs, projection cursor, claim/submission identity, and stale-write result.
- Keep queue saturation, shutdown, and generic S3 response permutations out of these runs.
- Assert no eager recovery deletion, archive the compact run evidence, then use test-only cleanup for the isolated prefix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The gated harness uses the pinned AWS SDK and selected general-purpose S3 environment from at least two independent host/process identities. (E05 AC6, AC9)
- [ ] Killing active controller A allows C to acquire a higher fence, rebuild/verify the exact current projection, process a sealed submission, and continue work without A returning. (E05 AC4, AC6)
- [ ] An E04 unexpired claim remains valid across the live controller replacement. (E05 AC6)
- [ ] In a separate pause/resume run, A exceeds its safe term, C takes over, and A's delayed stale head write is rejected after resume. (E05 AC3, AC9)
- [ ] Evidence includes head version/owner/fence/tail, fresh per-commit operation IDs, projection cursor, claim/submission identity, and stale-write result.
- [ ] Recovery performs no eager deletion; test-only cleanup occurs only after evidence capture and affects only the isolated prefix. (E05 AC9)
- [ ] The live task does not duplicate queue saturation, supervisor shutdown, or the generic E02 provider-error matrix.

## Testing Strategy

- **Unit/fixture:** none added beyond harness argument/environment validation; implementation behavior is already covered by Steps 1–7.
- **Live integration:** run the kill/failover/progress scenario and the independent pause/takeover/zombie-rejection scenario; preserve compact logs/artifacts needed to audit each assertion.
- **Failure handling:** skip/fail with an explicit reason when credentials, bucket isolation, or independent host identities are unavailable; never silently substitute an in-memory backend.
- **Manual review:** verify the two runs are independent, A is truly killed in the first and truly resumed in the second, no old-host cooperation is required, and cleanup is test-only.

title: Replay exact S3 ancestry and destructively rebuild invalid local state
description:
## Context

E03 reconstructs disposable SQLite state from the authoritative S3 head and immutable parent chain. Prefix listing cannot define history because unreferenced immutable objects can remain after races or failed publication.

The same replay path must handle a fresh machine, incremental catch-up, and destructive replacement of a locally invalid database. A remote history that does not contain a non-genesis local cursor is an authority conflict, not local corruption, and must never trigger automatic deletion/rebuild.

## Current State

The repository currently has only `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`, and the design documents; it has no code or Cargo configuration. `docs/mvp-outline.md` §6 defines the append-oriented head/event chain, §11 defines the sync sequence, §25 identifies controller crash/unknown-outcome cases, and §42 names `pi-campaign/src/sync/{head,event,replay}.rs`, `pi-campaign/src/db/schema.rs`, and `pi-campaign/src/storage/s3.rs`.

E02 (`ravel-aq8`) must land first with the direct AWS SDK S3 module, frozen v1 bytes/envelopes, digest verification, immutable event addressing, a checked-in complete parent-chain fixture, and concrete-client request capture/interception used by its own tests. If E02 lacks test request recording when this task starts, add narrow `#[cfg(test)]` instrumentation adjacent to the concrete client; do not introduce a storage trait or backend.

This task builds on the E03 converter, atomic apply operation, minimal schema, and single blocking SQLite worker.

## Desired State

One replay/startup operation:

1. Reads a fresh campaign head through E02's concrete S3 module.
2. Reads the local `(sequence, tail_digest)` cursor.
3. Traverses immutable events backward by exact parent key/sequence/digest.
4. For a genesis cursor, reaches genesis. For a non-genesis cursor, finds that exact `(sequence, digest)` in the traversed ancestry.
5. Fetches complete event bytes and completes E02 encoding/version/digest validation plus intrinsic E03 conversion for the entire unseen chain before sending any apply command. Preparation is bounded by a fixed private maximum unseen-event count and aggregate prepared-byte cap; exceeding either returns a typed replay overflow error before any apply command.
6. Reverses the prepared chain and applies events in ascending sequence through the one SQLite worker.
7. Returns a typed success with the observed fresh head and resulting local cursor, or a typed replay error. It does not own or persist readiness.

Reaching genesis without a non-genesis local cursor, finding the local cursor ahead of the head, or finding the same sequence under another digest returns a typed history conflict. It performs no apply and no automatic local rebuild.

At startup, local application/schema version, `quick_check`, applicable foreign keys, fixed cursor identity, contiguous applied-event prefix, and applied-tail/cursor equality are validated before local users can be served. A local validation failure closes and deletes the database, recreates the minimal schema, and invokes this same replay operation from genesis. Failure to verify remote history leaves the replacement unavailable; the old invalid database is never served or restored.

## Implementation Guidance

- Implement direct head/event traversal in `pi-campaign/src/sync/{head,event,replay}.rs`; call `pi-campaign/src/storage/s3.rs` directly.
- Do not call `ListObjects*` or infer the chain from prefix contents. Request instrumentation should prove only head/event `GET` calls occur.
- Validate every downloaded object's full bytes/version/digest using E02 before invoking the pure converter. Prepare the complete unseen chain before the first worker apply command, subject to the fixed private unseen-event-count and aggregate prepared-byte caps; overflow is a typed replay error, not partial apply. Add bounded temporary disk spooling only if the capped in-memory implementation fails the fresh-rebuild benchmark below.
- Compare local ancestry by both sequence and digest. A sequence-only match is not sufficient.
- Return typed categories for head read, missing object/link, version/encoding, digest, conversion, ancestry conflict, apply/database, and local-integrity failures. Do not update an atomic/SQLite readiness flag here.
- Put startup checks and destructive replacement beside `db/schema.rs` and `sync/replay.rs`; do not add `db/migrations.rs`, database repair, backup/restore, copy-from-peer, or a second recovery workflow.
- Narrow semantic local checks to cursor singleton and contiguous applied-event tail consistency. Do not attempt a generic semantic row validator.
- Reuse E02's live concrete-S3 evidence. Do not add a new credential-gated E03 suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [AC1] A fresh empty directory reconstructs a multi-event campaign by a fresh head read and complete parent traversal.
- [ ] [AC1] An incrementally synchronized database catches up only after traversal encounters its exact local sequence and digest.
- [ ] [AC1] An unreferenced event object is ignored and request traces contain no S3 `LIST` operation.
- [ ] [AC1/AC4] A valid remote fork that reaches genesis without the non-genesis local cursor returns history conflict, performs zero apply commands, leaves the valid local database unchanged, and does not auto-rebuild.
- [ ] [AC2] Every unseen event's full bytes, version, encoding, digest, and intrinsic conversion are verified before the first apply command.
- [ ] [AC2] Preparation enforces the fixed private maximum unseen-event count and aggregate prepared-byte cap; exceeding either returns a typed overflow error with zero apply commands.
- [ ] [AC2/AC4] Missing/corrupt links, unknown version, malformed encoding, digest mismatch, and conversion failure on any chain position send zero apply commands for that sync attempt.
- [ ] [AC4] Replay returns typed outcomes/errors; it neither persists nor directly marks readiness.
- [ ] [AC8/AC10] Startup validates application/schema version, `quick_check`, applicable foreign keys, fixed cursor identity, contiguous applied-event prefix, and cursor/tail equality.
- [ ] [AC10] A representative local version/integrity failure closes/deletes/recreates the database and invokes the same replay path from genesis.
- [ ] [AC10] Failed replacement replay never serves or restores the invalid prior database.
- [ ] No object-store trait/fake backend, migration/repair/backup/copy path, or new credential-gated E03 S3 suite is introduced.

## Testing Strategy

- **Fixture integration:** Use E02's checked-in multi-event chain for fresh replay, exact-ancestor catch-up, and orphan-object behavior.
- **Request/call tracing:** Assert head/event reads and no list call; count worker apply commands to prove zero on every pre-apply failure.
- **Fork fixture:** Build a fully valid alternate chain with the same genesis but without the non-genesis local cursor; assert conflict and unchanged local state.
- **Startup fixtures:** Use one application/schema version mismatch, one declared integrity failure, and one cursor/applied-tail inconsistency rather than a broad malformed-row matrix.
- **Rebuild tests:** Cover successful replacement and a replacement whose remote replay fails; verify the old invalid database never becomes available.
- **Rebuild benchmark:** Run one fresh-genesis rebuild at both the unseen-event-count and prepared-byte caps under the frozen process-memory limit; the capped in-memory path must pass, or bounded temporary spooling is required.
- **Integrity checks:** Run `quick_check` and applicable `foreign_key_check` on the successfully rebuilt file.
- **Manual review:** Confirm all S3 calls use E02's concrete module and no `LIST`, migration, backup, peer-copy, or second recovery mechanism exists.

## Design Gate

Design settled by docs/mvp-outline.md §11, §6; decomposed from epic ravel-1l4 via forged plan /home/ahrav/.claude/plans/2026-08-08-ravel-e03-tasks-v2.md. No separate design review required.

title: Gate readiness and expose only the immediate ready-work query
description:
## Context

After replay, controllers and workers need a fail-closed statement of which fresh S3 head the local projection matches. The immediate next milestone also needs the ready-work/dependency decision described in `docs/mvp-outline.md` §9.

E03 does not need a generic repository/query framework. Equal verified cursors must imply equivalent event-derived state for one concrete ready-work caller, while cache/advisory/occupancy state remains outside the schema.

## Current State

The repository currently has no code or Cargo configuration; root configuration is limited to `AGENTS.md`, `.gitignore`, and `.gitattributes`. `docs/epics.md` E03 requires verified cursor/readiness and equivalent event-derived query state. `docs/mvp-outline.md` §8 defines the small `WorkItem`, §9 defines ready work as dependencies satisfied, capabilities matching, and budget permitting execution, §11 says application queries are local, and §42 names `sync/{cursor,head,replay}.rs` and `db/projections.rs`.

This task builds on typed replay outcomes from the exact-ancestry replay/startup task and on the single SQLite worker. It must not move readiness into durable SQLite state.

## Desired State

A refresh/status operation returns either:

- `Ready { local_cursor, observed_head }`, only when the latest replay succeeded and the post-replay local `(sequence, tail_digest)` exactly equals the fresh head read by that attempt; or
- a typed `NotReady` reason for head-read, ancestry, version/digest/conversion, apply/database/integrity, behind/ahead, or tail mismatch.

Readiness is process-local and ephemeral. A later remote head advance makes the next fresh comparison not ready until replay catches up.

The only new production scheduling query is:

`list_ready_work(campaign_id, local_capabilities, limit, after)`

It reads SQLite only and returns results ordered by `(workflow_id, work_id)`. `after` is an optional stable `(workflow_id, work_id)` rotation key: results begin strictly after it in stable order and wrap around exactly once, so concurrent claimers colliding on the first page progress deterministically to later ready items. Claim state is not projected into this query. A row qualifies only when:

- its campaign and workflow are active;
- the work item's event-derived state is schedulable (not cancelled or terminal);
- its projected budget fields permit another execution;
- every dependency endpoint exists and is in the satisfied terminal state; and
- every required capability is present in `local_capabilities`.

No generic campaign/workflow/work CRUD or projection query interface is added.

## Implementation Guidance

- Keep cursor/head comparison in `pi-campaign/src/sync/{cursor,head,replay}.rs`; use the observed head returned by the replay attempt rather than performing an unrelated comparison.
- Step 5/replay errors are data. This layer alone maps them to ephemeral `NotReady` and clears prior ready state on every new failed refresh.
- Store no authoritative `ready` row/column in SQLite.
- Implement `list_ready_work` in `pi-campaign/src/db/projections.rs` and execute it through the one blocking worker.
- Make dependency satisfaction an all-dependencies condition. A missing dependency row is not satisfied.
- Normalize capability comparison to E02/domain capability values; do not introduce a policy DSL.
- Enforce a bounded caller-supplied `limit` and stable `(workflow_id, work_id)` ordering. Do not expose unspecified database row order. Support the optional `after` rotation key with a single wrap. Keep bounded per-process suppression of recently failed claim attempts in the caller/scheduler layer — ephemeral memory only, never in SQLite and never projected claim state.
- Add a test-only canonical dump that sorts every row of `applied_events`, `sync_cursor`, `campaigns`, `objectives`, `workflows`, `work_items`, and `dependencies`. It is not a production generic query API.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [AC4/AC5] `Ready` is returned only after successful replay when local sequence/digest exactly equals the fresh observed head.
- [ ] [AC4/AC5] Behind, ahead, tail mismatch, head-read failure, ancestry/version/digest/conversion failure, database/integrity failure, and prior failed refresh all return typed `NotReady`.
- [ ] [AC5] Advancing the remote head causes the next fresh comparison to report not ready until catch-up completes.
- [ ] [AC5] `list_ready_work(campaign_id, local_capabilities, limit, after)` reads no S3 state and returns stable `(workflow_id, work_id)` order.
- [ ] [AC5] With `after` set, results begin strictly after the rotation key and wrap exactly once; claim state remains unprojected and failed-claim suppression stays bounded, per-process, and outside SQLite.
- [ ] [AC5] The ready predicate requires active campaign/workflow, schedulable work state, projected budget admission, all dependencies satisfied, and required-capability inclusion.
- [ ] [AC5] A fresh replay and incremental replay at the same cursor produce identical ready-work results for representative campaign/capability/limit inputs.
- [ ] [AC5] A canonical stable-order dump of all seven in-scope tables is identical for fresh and incremental replay at the same cursor.
- [ ] [AC9] No artifact/advisory/presence state or generic campaign/workflow/work query framework is added or tested.
- [ ] Readiness remains ephemeral and is not treated as durable SQLite authority.

## Testing Strategy

- **Unit tests:** Map every typed replay/head/database outcome to ready or the expected not-ready reason.
- **Fixture integration:** Build one database incrementally and one from genesis to the same cursor; compare ready-work results across capability sets and limits.
- **Predicate table tests:** Cover unsatisfied/missing dependencies, inactive parents, terminal/cancelled work, denied budget, missing capability, all conditions satisfied, and deterministic limiting/order.
- **Canonical equivalence:** Compare every in-scope table row in stable order at the same cursor.
- **Contention:** Simulate concurrent claimers colliding on the first ready page and assert rotation plus bounded suppression progresses them deterministically to later ready items.
- **Fresh-head test:** Advance fixture head after a ready result and prove the next refresh fails closed until replay.
- **Manual review:** Confirm query execution is local-only and no cache/advisory mutation tests or generic query API were introduced.

## Design Gate

title: Prove crash-boundary and injected-write-failure recovery
description:
## Context

E03 must prove recovery at three different apply boundaries: no apply attempt, an uncommitted transaction, and a committed transaction whose success was not observed. Ordinary in-process hooks are insufficient because they do not prove that the child actually reached and remained at the cut or that the supervisor completed `SIGKILL` before restart.

This task adds only a focused subprocess harness and one narrow SQLite failure injection. It does not add a production failpoint framework or a subprocess-visible object-store backend.

## Current State

The repository currently has no implementation or Cargo configuration; root configuration is limited to `AGENTS.md`, `.gitignore`, and `.gitattributes`. `docs/epics.md` E03 requires kill and injected-write-failure coverage before apply, after row mutation/before commit, and immediately after commit. `docs/mvp-outline.md` §25 lists controller crash/unknown-outcome cases; §11 and §42 identify the projection, replay, and cursor modules under test.

This task depends on the real E03 schema, converter, atomic applier, single SQLite worker in `DELETE` journal mode, exact replay path, readiness gate, and E02's checked-in prepared event fixtures. Step 5 separately proves concrete S3 traversal, so this subprocess harness must not invent another storage abstraction.

## Desired State

A supervisor launches a child against a temporary file-backed database and checked-in prepared events. The child has exactly three test-only cut sites:

1. event prepared, immediately before the apply command begins;
2. event-derived rows mutated, before transaction commit; and
3. transaction committed, before the owned success response is delivered.

At a selected site, the child sends a distinct `REACHED:<site>` control message and blocks waiting for a release that the kill test never sends. The supervisor confirms the exact message, verifies the child remains blocked/alive, sends `SIGKILL`, waits until process termination is confirmed, and only then restarts/reopens the same database.

The post-commit test uses a separate externally observed response pipe/witness. The witness must show no success response arrived before the kill even though the internal control pipe proves the post-commit site was reached.

A separate test-only SQLite abort trigger forces a statement failure after event-derived row mutation and before commit. Production code gains no general failpoint registry.

## Implementation Guidance

- Put the harness in integration-test support; exercise the real `pi-campaign/src/db/projections.rs`, `sync/replay.rs`, and `sync/cursor.rs` paths.
- Use local checked-in E02 verified/prepared event bytes or values. Do not require credentials, a subprocess S3 fixture, an object-store trait, or a fake backend.
- Use two independent IPC channels for the post-commit case: an internal control handshake and the externally visible operation-response witness.
- Treat receipt of `REACHED` alone as insufficient. Assert the child remains alive/blocked, send `SIGKILL`, and inspect wait status before restart.
- At mid-transaction, place the cut after real scheduling row statements and before commit so SQLite's rollback journal is exercised.
- At post-commit, place the cut after commit returns and before any success send/ack visible to the caller.
- Keep phase hooks compile-time test-only and enumerate only these three sites.
- At each boundary assert narrow recovery invariants; run expensive integrity and full equivalence checks once after the final recovered state.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [AC11] The before-apply child proves the prepared site was reached/blocked, is killed and reaped before restart, and recovery applies the event exactly once.
- [ ] [AC11] The mid-transaction child proves the row-mutated/pre-commit site was reached/blocked; after kill/reopen no partial rows, applied event, or cursor advance remain, and recovery applies once.
- [ ] [AC11] The post-commit child proves commit completed but the external response witness observed no success before kill; recovery identifies the exact event and performs a no-op.
- [ ] [AC11] The injected SQLite statement failure rolls back event rows, applied-event insertion, and cursor advance, and readiness remains false until clean replay succeeds.
- [ ] [AC3/AC4] At every boundary, expected scheduling rows, singleton cursor, applied-event count, and readiness match uninterrupted replay with no skip or duplicate.
- [ ] [AC6] The harness exercises the real single worker/connection and confirms restart occurs only after child termination.
- [ ] [AC8/AC10] The final recovered database passes `quick_check`, applicable `foreign_key_check`, canonical table equivalence, and ready-work equivalence once.
- [ ] No production failpoint framework, object-store interface/backend, live credentials, or repeated full integrity/equivalence suite at every cut is introduced.

## Testing Strategy

- **Subprocess integration:** Run one supervisor/child case per cut site with unique handshake messages, liveness checks, `SIGKILL`, wait-status confirmation, and restart.
- **External witness:** For post-commit, poll/read the response witness before kill and assert no success; after restart, assert exact idempotent no-op behavior.
- **Injected-write failure:** Use a narrow test-only SQLite trigger/error at the required statement position and compare pre/post transaction state.
- **Boundary assertions:** Check rows, cursor, applied-event count, and readiness at each cut.
- **Final full check:** On one final recovered database, run SQLite integrity checks, canonical seven-table comparison, and ready-work equivalence against uninterrupted replay.
- **Manual review:** Confirm only three test sites exist and no production failpoint/storage abstraction or repeated full-check loop was added.

## Design Gate

title: Define claim identity, state, authority, and minimal presence
description:
## Context

Epic E04 needs a minimal domain model that makes a work claim authoritative without treating a machine heartbeat as ownership. The private Research and Change pilots need to distinguish a configured logical actor from each process incarnation, bind both to an exact `WorkItem.revision`, and carry a monotonic fence through completion.

This task establishes those types and the smallest advisory presence record. It deliberately avoids capability matching, a local presence projection, a membership framework, and a two-stage completion model.

## Current State

The repository currently has design documents and beads metadata but no Rust source. `docs/mvp-outline.md` §8 defines `WorkItem` and its `revision`; §9 defines the claim fields and same-key CAS model; §10 defines actor/instance identity and advisory presence. Section 42 names `pi-campaign/src/domain/work.rs`, `domain/attempt.rs`, `distributed/identity.rs`, `distributed/claims.rs`, and `distributed/presence.rs` as concrete module locations.

This task builds on E01's checked-in private actor/static-capability/S3 configuration and the one-package Rust runtime, record encoding conventions, and selected AWS SDK established by E02. E03 supplies the disposable work projection but must not store authoritative claim or presence state.

## Desired State

The package has distinct `ActorId` and `InstanceId` types. The actor comes from private pilot configuration; a fresh random instance ID is generated once for every process start and is never persisted for reuse.

A versioned claim record contains work ID, work revision, owner actor, owner instance, monotonic fence, stable operation ID, and exactly one state: `Active { lease_until }` or `Sealed { result_ref }`. There is no separate `Submitted` stage. A crate-private `ClaimAuthority` carries the exact work/revision, owner, fence, and opaque S3 object version proven by a successful claim mutation. It cannot be publicly constructed and does not implement `Clone`.

Presence can be published and read at `workspace/{workspace_id}/presence/{actor_id}/{instance_id}.json`. Its domain shape contains only actor, instance, configured static capabilities, and freshness. Missing, stale, expired, or malformed presence is treated as an absent scheduling hint and never as lost ownership.

## Implementation Guidance

- Place work/revision and result-reference domain pieces in `pi-campaign/src/domain/work.rs` and `pi-campaign/src/domain/attempt.rs` as appropriate to the E02 package layout.
- Put actor/instance construction in `pi-campaign/src/distributed/identity.rs`; generate the instance at process startup rather than on each claim.
- Put the concrete versioned claim record and `ClaimAuthority` in `pi-campaign/src/distributed/claims.rs`. Keep authority fields private to the module and do not add a public raw-parts constructor.
- Put the minimal S3 presence record in `pi-campaign/src/distributed/presence.rs`. Do not add ownership, assignments, fences, dynamic load, completion state, capability scoring/matching, or a SQLite presence table.
- Follow E02's private versioned-envelope and fail-closed decoding conventions. Reject unknown versions, invalid IDs, zero/invalid fences, missing operation identity, invalid expiry, a terminal state without `result_ref`, and a result reference on an active state before conversion to domain types.
- Keep fence arithmetic concrete to claim transitions and checked for overflow. Section 42 names `distributed/fencing.rs`, but this task does not require a reusable fencing abstraction.
- Keep presence freshness outside all claim and recovery APIs. A reader may report a usable hint or absence; it must not mutate claim state.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **E04 AC1:** `ActorId` and `InstanceId` are distinct types, and two process starts for the same actor produce different instance IDs.
- [ ] **E04 AC1:** Every decoded active or sealed claim binds work ID, work revision, actor, instance, fence, and operation ID.
- [ ] **E04 AC1/AC5:** The claim state has exactly one terminal variant, `Sealed { result_ref }`; there is no `Active -> Submitted -> Sealed` pipeline.
- [ ] **E04 AC4:** `ClaimAuthority` is crate-private/non-publicly constructible, contains the exact claim generation and opaque object version, and is non-`Clone`.
- [ ] **E04 AC2:** The serialized presence shape contains only actor, instance, configured static capabilities, and freshness.
- [ ] **E04 AC2:** Missing, stale, expired, or malformed presence becomes an absent advisory hint and cannot alter or invalidate a claim.
- [ ] No generic membership/lease framework, capability matcher, presence SQLite projection, public provider/worker API, or new crate is introduced.
- [ ] Versioned claim and presence fixtures fail closed on malformed or unknown records before domain conversion.

## Testing Strategy

- **Unit:** Verify per-start instance uniqueness for a fixed actor, identity type separation, non-wrapping fence validation, and active/sealed state invariants.
- **Fixture:** Check in private v1 claim and presence fixtures; round-trip valid records and reject unknown versions, malformed identity/revision/fence/operation fields, and illegal state/result combinations.
- **Unit:** Test presence freshness classification with explicit timestamps, including missing and malformed records, without touching claim state.
- **Manual review:** Inspect public exports and trait impls to confirm `ClaimAuthority` has no raw constructor or `Clone`, and inspect the presence schema for prohibited ownership/dynamic fields. Rust privacy is sufficient; do not add a compile-fail harness.

## Design Gate
Design settled by docs/mvp-outline.md §8, §9, §10; decomposed from epic ravel-vsg via forged plan /home/ahrav/.claude/plans/2026-08-08-ravel-e04-tasks-v2.md. No separate design review required.

title: Acquire claims and gate execution with retained fence state
description:
## Context

Epic E04 requires the first claimant for a work item to win through S3 create-if-absent and to receive an authority value only when durable state proves that win. This is the first place where an ambiguous network response could otherwise let two machines believe they own the same work.

The Research and Change pilots also need a concrete execution boundary that cannot be entered by supplying plausible raw actor, instance, revision, or fence values. Claim history must remain present because key absence is used only for a never-before-claimed work item.

## Current State

The repository is currently design-only. `docs/mvp-outline.md` §9 specifies the read, absent/reclaimable check, fence increment, and S3 conditional write. E04 Step 1 will provide the versioned claim record, distinct identities, and non-`Clone` crate-private `ClaimAuthority`.

E02 is expected to provide `pi-campaign/src/storage/s3.rs` with direct AWS SDK `If-None-Match`/`If-Match` calls, opaque ETags, stable-operation retry rules, response-loss hooks, selected-bucket integration tests, and an application role with no deletion path for its existing durable prefixes. E03 provides verified current `WorkItem` data. Claim and submission prefixes were not covered by E02's retention criterion, so this task extends the selected environment for claim keys.

## Desired State

Given a verified current `WorkItem` and no existing claim object, the claims module writes one versioned `Active` record to `workspace/{workspace_id}/campaigns/{campaign_id}/work/{work_id}/claim.json` using `If-None-Match: *`. It starts at fence 1 and binds the current revision, local actor/instance, exact initial lease expiry, and stable operation ID.

The caller receives `ClaimAuthority` only after S3 confirms success or a same-key reread proves that the exact operation, bytes, owner, revision, fence, and opaque ETag committed. A collision, another operation, or unresolved evidence returns no authority. The internal execution-start API requires the authority, verifies its work ID/revision against the `WorkItem`, and accepts no raw authority fields. It performs the gate without retaining or cloning the authority, leaving one worker-side owner available for renewal and eventual sealing.

Retained campaign claim keys cannot disappear: application code has no delete/GC path, lifecycle rules do not expire the prefix, and runtime credentials cannot call `DeleteObject` successfully on it.

## Implementation Guidance

- Implement acquisition in `pi-campaign/src/distributed/claims.rs` using E02's direct selected-S3 support in `pi-campaign/src/storage/s3.rs`; do not add an object-store trait or fake backend.
- Construct the claim key from trusted workspace/campaign/work IDs. Validate that the key's work ID and the record's work ID/revision match the verified `WorkItem`.
- Use fence 1 only for an absent retained key. Never treat a typed precondition failure as success and never overwrite an existing key during acquisition.
- Generate one operation ID before the request. Any E02-managed safe retry must preserve identical canonical bytes, `If-None-Match: *`, and operation ID.
- For timeout/reset/lost success, GET the same key. Return authority only if the durable record exactly matches the attempted operation, owner, work/revision, fence, state, and bytes; attach only the ETag returned by that read/write.
- If the reread shows another record, return a collision/observed-state result for later renewal/reclamation logic. If evidence is incomplete, return an explicit unresolved outcome, not guessed authority.
- Add one concrete crate-internal execution-start function at the worker entry point established by E02. It should require `&ClaimAuthority` for the initial check, return an execution future/handle that does not retain the borrow, and reject a revision mismatch before work starts. Do not create a generic worker, workflow, provider, or plugin trait.
- Extend the existing selected-S3 lifecycle/IAM configuration rather than creating new infrastructure machinery. Production runtime code must expose no claim deletion/GC operation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **E04 AC1/AC3:** An absent retained claim key is created as `Active` with `If-None-Match: *`, fence 1, current work revision, local actor/instance, lease expiry, and stable operation ID.
- [ ] **E04 AC3/AC7:** Two independent claimant instances racing on one absent key cannot both receive valid `ClaimAuthority`; exactly one durable record wins.
- [ ] **E04 AC9:** Lost/ambiguous claim responses are resolved by a same-key reread; authority is returned only for an exact committed-operation match.
- [ ] Typed `409`/`412` or another durable operation returns no authority, and an unresolved reread remains explicitly unresolved.
- [ ] **E04 AC4:** The concrete execution-start API requires `ClaimAuthority`, rejects a work/revision mismatch before execution, and has no overload accepting raw actor, instance, revision, or fence values.
- [ ] The execution-start check neither clones nor retains authority; one concrete worker-side owner remains responsible for later claim mutations.
- [ ] Claim keys for retained campaigns have no application deletion/GC, no matching lifecycle expiration, and no runtime `DeleteObject` permission.
- [ ] Acquisition uses E02's direct AWS SDK boundary and adds no generic storage, lease, membership, or worker framework.

## Testing Strategy

- **Unit/fixture:** Verify canonical acquisition bytes, trusted key construction, fence 1, exact authority fields/ETag, and execution rejection for one revision mismatch.
- **Fault fixture:** Cover no-commit timeout/reset, committed-but-response-lost, exact-operation reread, another-operation reread, and unresolved evidence. Assert that a mere attempted PUT never yields authority.
- **Live integration:** Race two actor/instance pairs against one isolated absent key with the pinned SDK; assert one create succeeds and only that generation receives authority. Exercise typed precondition behavior through E02's hooks.
- **Live configuration:** Query the selected bucket lifecycle configuration to confirm no rule expires the claim prefix, attempt deletion with runtime credentials and require denial, then reread the claim to prove it remains.
- **Manual review:** Search production paths for claim `DeleteObject`, alternate claim keys, raw execution authority parameters, and object-store abstractions; all must be absent.

## Design Gate

title: Renew and reclaim claims with fixed lease and revision supersession
description:
## Context

Epic E04 must allow long-running work to renew, dead workers' claims to be reclaimed, and newer work revisions to make progress without allowing an old generation to regain authority. Every mutation must contend on the same claim ETag and advance one monotonic fence.

A terminal result for an old revision is a special correctness case: it has no lease to expire, so leaving it immutable would strand the newer revision forever. The minimal fix is a same-key conditional supersession, not another key or a generic lease service.

## Current State

The repository currently has no code. E04 Steps 1-2 will provide the versioned `Active`/`Sealed` claim record, non-`Clone` `ClaimAuthority`, create-if-absent acquisition, concrete execution gating, and retained claim keys. E03 supplies a freshly verified current `WorkItem.revision`; E02 supplies direct S3 `If-Match`, response-loss hooks, and opaque ETags.

`docs/mvp-outline.md` §9 requires renewal by CAS and reclamation by checked fence advancement. E04 acceptance criteria require one frozen lease policy, lower-fence/wrong-revision rejection, controller-independent active claims, and fault coverage for lost renewal responses and worker death.

## Desired State

The claims module contains one private pilot lease policy as code constants: a 15-minute claim lease and a 5-minute renewal cadence. There is no config field or reusable lease engine. `now < lease_until` is unexpired; at `now >= lease_until`, renewal is refused and expiry reclamation may proceed. A successful renewal proposes `now + 15 minutes` and succeeds only when that timestamp is strictly later than the observed expiry.

Renewal consumes the current `ClaimAuthority`. It returns a refreshed authority only after a matching same-key `If-Match` succeeds or a reread proves the exact renewal operation committed. An unconfirmed ambiguous response never creates a later local expiry. Renewal also refuses when the freshly verified projected work revision differs from the authority/claim revision.

An expired active claim can be replaced on its observed ETag by `Active` for the new actor/instance and current revision at checked `fence + 1`. A sealed claim for an older revision can likewise be superseded immediately on its observed ETag, preventing stale terminal state from blocking current work. A sealed claim for the current revision remains terminal. Two replacements racing from one ETag produce one authority.

## Implementation Guidance

- Keep policy constants and concrete transitions in `pi-campaign/src/distributed/claims.rs`; call E02's `pi-campaign/src/storage/s3.rs` directly. Do not add configuration parsing or a lease trait/service.
- Use the timestamp representation already established by E02 records. Perform checked timestamp addition and checked fence addition; overflow fails closed.
- Renewal input must include the freshly verified current `WorkItem` or revision evidence from E03. Require exact work ID/revision, actor, instance, fence, `Active` state, and authority ETag before attempting `If-Match`.
- Consume authority on renewal. Return a new authority with only the ETag and expiry proven by the committed record. On precondition failure, revision change, expiry, terminal state, or unresolved ambiguity, do not return the old authority as if refreshed.
- For ambiguous renewal, reread the same key. Exact operation/generation match returns the durable refreshed authority. An unchanged original record may be reported as not renewed only with its observed original expiry; no path may use the attempted future expiry until it is durable.
- Expiry reclaim requires `now >= lease_until`. Replace the exact observed ETag with the current work revision, new actor/instance, a new stable operation ID, and checked `fence + 1`.
- Revision supersession is allowed only when a freshly verified current `WorkItem` has the same work ID and a different revision from a `Sealed` record. It uses `If-Match` on that terminal record and checked `fence + 1`; it does not delete history or use `If-None-Match`.
- Leave an unexpired current-revision active claim unchanged regardless of controller restart or fresh/stale/missing presence. No machine-departure event is consulted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **E04 AC3:** The only lease constants are a private 15-minute duration and 5-minute renewal cadence; there is no runtime policy/config surface or generic lease framework.
- [ ] **E04 AC3/AC4:** Renewal consumes a matching non-`Clone` authority, performs same-key `If-Match`, and returns a refreshed authority only for a proven committed renewal.
- [ ] A successful renewal writes `now + 15 minutes` only when it strictly exceeds the observed expiry; at `now >= lease_until`, renewal fails and reclamation is eligible.
- [ ] **E04 AC9:** A lost renewal response is resolved by reread, and an unconfirmed renewal never synthesizes or exposes the attempted later expiry.
- [ ] Renewal fails closed for wrong actor, instance, work ID, projected revision, fence, ETag, expiry, or terminal state.
- [ ] **E04 AC3/AC7:** Expired active reclamation uses same-key `If-Match`, checked `fence + 1`, the current revision, and the replacement actor/instance; two reclaimers cannot both receive authority.
- [ ] **E04 AC1/AC7:** A stale-revision `Sealed` claim can be superseded on its ETag by `Active(current_revision, fence + 1)`, while a current-revision terminal claim cannot be reclaimed.
- [ ] **E04 AC8:** An unexpired current-revision active claim survives controller replacement and stale/missing presence unchanged.
- [ ] **E04 AC9:** Worker death requires lease expiry and same-key reclamation only; no presence deletion or machine-departure event is required.

## Testing Strategy

- **Unit:** Use explicit timestamps to test renewal before expiry, exact expiry (`now == lease_until`), after expiry, strict extension, checked timestamp/fence overflow, and 15-minute/5-minute constants.
- **Unit/fixture:** Reject each owner/revision/fence/ETag/state mismatch. Include the required freshly verified revision mismatch that prevents an old worker from renewing.
- **Fault fixture:** Inject committed-but-response-lost and not-committed renewal outcomes. Assert only the durable reread expiry is returned and no candidate expiry is guessed.
- **Live integration:** Race two actor/instance pairs from one expired active ETag and from one stale-revision terminal ETag; assert one higher-fence active generation wins in each case.
- **Integration:** Simulate worker death by ceasing renewal, advance to the exact reclaim boundary with explicit test time, and reclaim without changing or deleting presence.
- **Manual review:** Confirm every mutation uses the claim key's observed ETag, every increment is checked, and no side key, departure event, or lease abstraction grants authority.

## Design Gate
