title: Implement the bounded Change migration contract and trusted discovery
description:
## Context

E01's Change pilot needs a finite semantic migration whose completeness can be measured mechanically. Repeating one deterministic query is not enough: the pilot also needs known positive/negative behavior, an independent inventory audit, trusted evaluators, safe scopes, and a completion rule that cannot overlook unresolved legacy targets.

Task 1 established only migration viability. This task turns that bounded candidate into the complete, tested Change contract without building a migration DSL, generic target framework, or runtime evaluator service.

## Current State

The repository has no Rust runtime and no Change configuration. `docs/mvp-outline.md` §18 defines the protocol-specific target fields, one-treatment migration shape, autonomous classification/grouping, and final rediscovery; §43 requires trusted evaluator isolation and forbids campaign completion without final rediscovery. Epic `ravel-q3w` requires deterministic discovery, explicit scopes, several dozen targets, and few or no subjective exemptions.

Task 1 provides `pilot/e01/environment.yaml`, `pilot/e01/preflight.sh`, and `pilot/e01/preflight.md`: the frozen revision, trust-root prefixes, numeric repository limits, baseline evaluator allowlist, and a passed Change cardinality/treatment/scope viability gate. There is no prior-epic code to extend.

## Desired State

Create:

- `pilot/e01/change/contract.md`
- `pilot/e01/change/discover.sh`
- `pilot/e01/change/targets.jsonl`
- `pilot/e01/change/fixtures/` with mandatory positive and negative fixtures

The artifacts fix one semantic treatment, deterministic trusted discovery, trusted evaluators, explicit candidate write scopes, a revision-bound inventory of several dozen targets, objective exemptions, an orthogonal inventory audit, and a final completion rule requiring zero non-exempt unresolved legacy targets.

## Implementation Guidance

Keep `Target` protocol-specific as required by `docs/mvp-outline.md` §18. Do not introduce alternate treatments, subjective exemption workflows, plugin hooks, a migration DSL, a universal target API, or a generic evaluator runner.

`discover.sh` must emit stable records containing:

- source revision
- discovery-rule digest
- target ID
- path
- semantic locator
- context digest

`targets.jsonl` must contain the frozen discovery output at the selected revision and several dozen targets. Every target must use the same fixed treatment. Define target-ID and context-digest inputs precisely enough that two runs at the same revision compare field-for-field.

`contract.md` must define:

- The semantic before/after treatment and objective resolved condition.
- Candidate write-scope allowlists. Validate every scope against Task 1 trust-root prefixes and numeric file/path limits.
- Trusted discovery and evaluator commands, expected verdicts, code/input/parser/control/baseline identities, and the rule that deterministic failure overrides model consensus.
- A short objective exemption list. No catch-all, discretionary, or “review later” exemption.
- A mandatory positive fixture with a known legacy target and expected discovery/evaluator result.
- A mandatory negative fixture with a similar non-target and expected non-discovery/preservation result.
- An independent inventory audit that uses an orthogonal repository search or manual inventory method and does not call or reproduce `discover.sh`. Reconcile every discrepancy as a target, objective exemption, or rule defect corrected before completion.
- Final rediscovery semantics. Campaign completion is allowed only when rediscovery reports zero non-exempt unresolved legacy targets. “Classified but unresolved” is not completion.

Keep discovery and evaluator material outside candidate write scopes. Candidate scopes must also exclude code-host workflow paths and any hidden evaluator inputs, expected outputs, parsers, controls, or baselines named in Task 1.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `contract.md` fixes exactly one semantic treatment and one objective resolved condition. **(E01 AC2)**
- [ ] `discover.sh` is trusted, revision-bound, and emits source revision, rule digest, target ID, path, semantic locator, and context digest. **(E01 AC2)**
- [ ] Two runs at the same revision produce identical rule digest, IDs, paths, locators, context digests, and count. **(E01 AC2)**
- [ ] `targets.jsonl` contains several dozen targets and every target uses the same treatment. **(E01 AC2)**
- [ ] Candidate write scopes are explicit, within Task 1 numeric limits, and disjoint from evaluator/workflow trust roots. **(E01 AC2/AC3)**
- [ ] Trusted Change evaluator commands and expected verdicts are fixed; deterministic failure cannot be overridden by model consensus. **(E01 AC4 and `docs/mvp-outline.md` §43)**
- [ ] Mandatory positive and negative fixtures pass their predeclared discovery and evaluator expectations. **(E01 AC2)**
- [ ] The orthogonal inventory audit is recorded and has no unexplained discrepancy with the final inventory. **(E01 AC2)**
- [ ] Every exemption is enumerated and objective; there is no catch-all or reviewer-discretion exemption. **(E01 AC2)**
- [ ] A controlled final-rediscovery check proves any remaining non-exempt unresolved legacy target blocks completion, and only zero permits completion. **(E01 AC2 and §43 invariant 17)**
- [ ] No migration DSL, target framework, plugin system, evaluator runner, public API, or runtime module is added. **(E01 AC8)**

## Testing Strategy

- **Unit:** If `discover.sh` contains nontrivial parsing helpers, test those with direct shell fixtures only; do not add a test framework.
- **Fixture:** Run the mandatory positive fixture through discovery and evaluators; run the similar negative fixture and prove it is not targeted or mutated. Run a controlled resolved case and a remaining-legacy case through final rediscovery.
- **Live integration:** Execute discovery twice and the trusted baseline/migration evaluators against the frozen repository revision in the preflighted Linux environment.
- **Manual review:** Perform the orthogonal inventory audit, reconcile every discrepancy, inspect exemptions, and verify all concrete scopes are disjoint from Task 1 trust roots and within numeric limits.

## Design Gate

title: Precommit the budgeted A/B/C experiments and record pilot identity
description:
## Context

E01 must precommit the Research and Change comparisons before measured pilot runs. A/B/C labels alone are insufficient because agent counts, assignment, visibility, communication, integration, reset semantics, treatment order, stopping, and treatment of failed runs can materially change the experiment.

This task also closes the private pilot configuration with fixed scalar budgets and immutable Git/content identity. It must use direct repository tools, not create a bundle subsystem, schema, validator, statistics framework, or runtime machinery.

## Current State

The repository has no runtime code or experiment framework. `docs/mvp-outline.md` §32 fixes the Research and Change treatments and measurement sets; §3 defers statistical performance search and generic workflow machinery; §43 requires bounded recursive work, hard budget enforcement, final rediscovery, actual multi-machine execution, and failover.

Task 1 provides the frozen environment, authority, trust roots, numeric repository limits, and passing preflight. Task 2 provides `pilot/e01/research.md` with the blinded reference/grading contract. Task 3 provides the fixed Change treatment, trusted discovery/evaluators, scopes, fixtures, target inventory, and final rediscovery rule. There are no prior-epic runtime outputs.

## Desired State

Create:

- `pilot/e01/budgets.yaml`
- `pilot/e01/experiments.md`

`budgets.yaml` contains fixed numeric caps for the eight E01 resource dimensions and explicit hard-limit behavior. `experiments.md` fully specifies all six Research/Change A/B/C cells, the treatment schedule, experimental and analysis units, isolation/reset rules, outcomes/calculations, and success/failure/inconclusive decisions. After committing all `pilot/e01/` artifacts, record the final Git revision, direct content digest, and one clean-checkout smoke result in task completion evidence outside the hashed directory.

## Implementation Guidance

Keep budgets flat. Give a numeric value and unit for exactly these mandatory dimensions:

1. calls or tokens
2. attempts
3. parallelism
4. generated follow-ups
5. workflow depth
6. deadlines
7. artifact size
8. total campaign spend or usage

Add a subordinate scalar only when one selected pilot concretely needs it to make a mandatory cap enforceable. Do not create campaign/workflow/work-item/provider/oracle budget hierarchies by default. Define the treatment/application unit and analysis unit. Use a complete assigned run as the independent unit unless another unit is explicitly justified; nested targets, work items, or conclusions are not independent replicates merely because there are many of them.

Use a seed-recorded blocked/counterbalanced schedule across A/B/C, or document a justified fixed-order model. Crashes, errors, and timeouts remain assigned treatment outcomes and are not discarded, retried as fresh observations, or silently replaced.

title: Reconstruct Disposable Local State from Durable History
description:
## Description

Build the per-node SQLite projection needed for synchronization and the next scheduling milestones. S3 remains the only durable authority. SQLite and the digest-addressed local artifact directory are disposable local accelerators and are never copied between machines.

A node rebuilds by reading a fresh campaign head and traversing immutable parent references, not by treating S3 prefix listing as a publication snapshot. Remote I/O and digest verification happen outside short database transactions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A fresh node reconstructs the campaign from the head by traversing the complete immutable parent chain; `LIST` is reserved for diagnosis or orphan accounting.
- [ ] Event bytes are fetched, version-validated, and digest-verified before opening the apply transaction.
- [ ] One transaction validates the next sequence and previous digest, applies all event-derived changes, records the unique event identity, and advances the `(sequence, tail_digest)` cursor.
- [ ] Reapplying the same event is a no-op. A gap, conflicting digest, unknown version, or failed conversion leaves both projection and cursor unchanged and makes readiness fail closed.
- [ ] The projector exposes its verified cursor against a freshly read S3 head. At the same cursor, all event-derived query state is equivalent; cache occupancy, advisory presence, and other ephemeral metadata are excluded.
- [ ] One daemon-owned writer task/connection serializes SQLite writes. No transaction or database guard crosses an `.await`, network work stays outside transactions, and blocking SQLite work does not run on async executor threads.
- [ ] The initial implementation uses serialized/default-journal access. WAL is enabled only after measured reader blocking justifies it, with one-host sidecars, writer-owned checkpointing, bounded busy handling, and verification of the linked SQLite version.
- [ ] The minimal schema has an explicit application/schema version and `NOT NULL` or `UNIQUE` constraints for stable identities, applied events, and cursors. If foreign keys are used, every connection enables and verifies them; rebuilt test databases pass `quick_check` and `foreign_key_check`.
- [ ] Only event/cursor and scheduling tables required by the current milestone are created; Research, Change, judgment, and evaluation tables arrive with their owning epics, with no generic projector, checkpoint, or cache-metadata framework.
- [ ] SQLite contains no uniquely durable state. Version or integrity mismatch stops local users and rebuilds from S3 instead of invoking online/rollback migrations, backup transport, or power-loss durability machinery.
- [ ] Kill and injected-write-failure tests cover before apply, after row mutation but before commit, and immediately after commit; recovery never skips or duplicates an event and never reports controller readiness from an invalid projection.

title: Prove the Trusted Evaluation and Code-Host Path
description:
## Description

Use the selected code host's existing CI matrices, trusted runner labels, required checks, and merge machinery as the primary distributed evaluation and integration path. Retain only a thin trusted wrapper for hidden deterministic commands and a publisher/reconciler for candidate refs, the single campaign branch, and the single campaign PR.

Evaluator execution remains a separate trust domain from candidate generation. The candidate may not alter evaluator/workflow definitions, hidden inputs, parsers, controls, or baselines. Ravel records exact commit and check-run identities but does not build an evaluator plugin platform, custom queue, or merge planner.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A fixed evaluator allowlist and exact-match capability labels select the trusted CI/runner jobs; there is no capability scoring, dynamic plugin loading, arbitrary evaluator DAG, or model-authored manifest.
- [ ] Each evaluation binds the exact candidate tree/commit, evaluator identity/version, trusted inputs, and policy and yields immutable `PASS`, `FAIL`, `ERROR`, or `TIMEOUT` evidence.
- [ ] Hidden evaluator commands run with immutable hidden inputs, no model access, no network inside the evaluated subprocess, separate writable state, fixed resource/output limits, and process-group kill/reap semantics.
- [ ] Candidate write policy prevents changes to evaluator and workflow paths, and trusted code verifies those inputs before accepting a check result.
- [ ] Required heterogeneous checks can run on remote hosts through existing code-host CI or trusted self-hosted labels; deterministic failure cannot be overridden by semantic judges.
- [ ] Only trusted publisher workers hold code-host credentials. Candidate refs, commit SHA, check-run identity, campaign branch, and campaign PR are recorded in campaign history.
- [ ] Branch push and PR create/update use deterministic external identities and reconcile timeout/lost-response outcomes by reading code-host state before retrying.
- [ ] Accepted non-overlapping candidates can be applied serially to one campaign branch and one campaign PR, after which existing required checks and merge queue or auto-merge perform integration.
- [ ] Fault tests cover evaluator timeout/crash, push success with lost response, duplicate PR request, stale check result, and publisher restart without duplicate authoritative integration.
- [ ] No custom CI service, general code-host interface, custom merge queue, review UI, or per-candidate PR fan-out is built.

title: Fence Campaign Authority and Controller Failover
description:
## Description

Make controller ownership and event publication one atomic CAS domain. The campaign head contains controller owner, lease, fence, event tail, and operation identity together. Acquisition, renewal, takeover, and every authoritative event commit conditionally replace that same object, preventing a stale controller from publishing through an independently observed log-head ETag.

Keep policy separate from authority: deterministic policy proposes transitions from immutable observations, while the fenced authority layer performs and validates S3 changes. The top-level node supervisor owns all long-lived loops, spawned tasks, and bounded admission points.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Controller owner, lease, monotonic fence, event tail, and operation identity reside in one versioned campaign-head object.
- [ ] Acquisition, renewal, takeover, and event publication all CAS the same observed head ETag; authoritative commit APIs require an opaque controller-authority value and revalidate it in that CAS.
- [ ] Event commits preserve the exact parent chain and cannot regress the controller fence. A stale controller cannot commit after a higher fence has won, even if it retained an older head observation.
- [ ] Before its first authoritative decision, a replacement controller rebuilds and verifies its projection to the exact freshly read S3 head. Gaps, unknown versions, and chain failures prevent readiness.
- [ ] Controller policy performs no S3 or provider I/O and cannot bypass the fenced commit layer; it only proposes deterministic state transitions.
- [ ] Killing the active controller allows another host to take over, process sealed submissions, and continue unexpired claims without requiring the old host to return.
- [ ] The node supervisor bounds every local admission queue and owns every renewal, sync, scheduling, invocation, and publication task. No detached task survives its owner.
- [ ] Shutdown stops admission, requests loop cancellation, classifies interrupted remote effects as known or unknown, performs required reconciliation, and joins or reaps all tasks before exit.
- [ ] Fault tests include lost head-CAS success followed by supersession, a delayed stale-controller write after takeover, takeover from stale SQLite, failure during submission processing, and restart reconciliation with no eager orphan deletion.

title: Isolate Candidates and Construct Immutable Git Artifacts
description:
## Description

Establish the local Change trust boundary independently of model, lease, and scheduler machinery. On the controlled Linux pilot, generated code runs in an existing OS sandbox against an exact source base. Trusted code validates a deliberately narrow filesystem delta and uses the Git CLI to construct an immutable candidate.

The MVP supports regular files, directories, and required executable-bit changes under explicit write scopes. It fails closed on repository and filesystem shapes the pilot does not need rather than implementing a general canonicalizer or sandbox backend.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Candidate execution has no daemon/code-host credentials, hidden evaluator material, writable daemon Git metadata, shared writable caches, or network access.
- [ ] An existing Linux isolation mechanism supplies read-only source/input binds, a private writable overlay and temporary directory, and fixed CPU, memory, process, time, filesystem, and output limits; no custom sandbox runtime or pluggable backend is built.
- [ ] Candidate and evaluator launch specifications are distinct concrete policy types and cannot be substituted for one another.
- [ ] The runner owns a process group, bounds stdout/stderr, and kills and reaps descendants before cleaning or reusing a workspace.
- [ ] Trusted validation accepts only regular-file additions, changes, deletions, directories, and allowed executable-bit changes inside the declared write scope and count/size caps.
- [ ] Symlinks, hard links, special files, nested repositories, submodules, LFS pointers, normalization/case ambiguity, unsupported modes, and any out-of-scope path fail closed before or after generation.
- [ ] Trusted Git commands construct an immutable candidate from the exact validated bytes and record base OID, result tree OID, candidate commit OID, and a transferable artifact; candidate identity binds to those Git identities plus the bundle digest, with no separate delta digest or bespoke delta serialization.
- [ ] Another machine reconstructs the exact candidate and verifies its identities without trusting the generator's report.
- [ ] A fresh repair attempt receives a new attempt and candidate identity. Rebase support and rename detection are omitted from the MVP rather than mutating prior evidence.
- [ ] Timeout, cancellation, blocked-pipe, and descendant-process tests prove workspace cleanup occurs only after all candidate processes are reaped.

title: Establish the S3 Durable Log and Minimal Rust Runtime
description:
## Description

Create one Cargo package producing one node binary and implement the narrow Amazon S3 correctness boundary used by the campaign: immutable create-if-absent objects and one conditionally replaced campaign head. Events and artifacts are immutable; publication authority resides only in the head. The implementation uses the selected AWS SDK directly and does not hide S3 behind a portable object-store abstraction.

Durable records use one explicit v1 event/head envelope and canonical bytes. The campaign is append-only for the MVP: retained history, leaked orphan objects, and bounded single-request artifacts are preferable to unsafe cleanup, compaction, or multipart machinery.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A pinned Rust toolchain, edition, async runtime, target set, and locked dependency set build one binary; CI runs formatting, check, clippy with warnings denied, and tests without repository credentials.
- [ ] Immutable events and artifacts are created with `If-None-Match: *`; initial head creation uses the same precondition; head replacement uses `If-Match` with the observed ETag.
- [ ] ETags are treated only as opaque version tokens. Existing immutable keys are accepted only after trusted full-byte SHA-256 and size verification.
- [ ] The versioned envelope records stable commit/operation identity, sequence, parent sequence/digest/key, writer fence, and canonical content; unknown versions or invalid encodings fail closed before conversion to domain types.
- [ ] A frozen v1 history fixture proves decode, digest, and chain behavior without introducing a schema framework.
- [ ] Ambiguous publication checks the current head and, if superseded, walks the complete retained parent chain for the operation identity. A gap remains `UNRESOLVED`, and no object is eagerly deleted.
- [ ] Two processes racing from one observed head produce at most one authoritative publication; stale ETags, duplicate puts, timeout/reset, lost success, and an ambiguous retry followed by `409` or `412` cannot corrupt the chain.
- [ ] Live integration tests against the selected general-purpose S3 bucket and pinned SDK exercise typed `404`, `409`, `412`, timeout/reset, and lost-response behavior. Publication retries are disabled or proven to preserve identical bytes, preconditions, and operation identity.
- [ ] A lower fixture fence cannot replace a higher-fence head; dynamic controller acquisition and stale-controller takeover are deferred to the controller-authority epic.
- [ ] Event, artifact, and head prefixes have no application deletion, GC, compaction, or lifecycle expiration. Pilot artifacts stay below the single-`PutObject` limit; multipart upload is deferred.

title: Fix the Pilot and Experiment Contracts
description:
## Description

Choose the two controlled pilots before building runtime machinery: one evidence-rich Research question and one finite Change migration with a trusted discovery rule, one fixed treatment, and several dozen targets. Check in private, unstable pilot configuration that fixes trust boundaries, safe repositories and branches, provider profiles, evaluator commands, scalar budgets, and precommitted experiment criteria.

The configuration is an input to the MVP, not a new product surface. It is versioned by Git revision and content digest and uses fixed enums, allowlists, and bounds rather than a policy language or compatibility framework.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The Research question has independently inspectable evidence and a defined method for assessing supported, incorrect, omitted, and unresolved conclusions.
- [ ] The Change migration has trusted deterministic discovery, one fixed treatment, explicit write scopes, several dozen targets, and few or no subjective exemptions.
- [ ] The pilot repository passes a Linux preflight and excludes unsupported repository constructs and candidate-controlled evaluator or workflow paths.
- [ ] One safe code host, repository, campaign branch policy, authority boundary, two model providers, fixed model profiles, trusted evaluator commands, and S3 environment are selected.
- [ ] Fixed caps cover calls or tokens, attempts, parallelism, follow-ups, workflow depth, deadlines, artifact size, and total campaign spend or usage.
- [ ] Inputs, run counts, outcomes, and success criteria are precommitted for the single-agent, single-machine multi-agent, and distributed treatments.
- [ ] Routine Research decisions and safe-branch Change integration are autonomous; any human-only boundary is explicit and outside ordinary pilot progress.
- [ ] The configuration format is private and unstable. No schema migration system, profile registry, policy DSL, public configuration API, or generic workflow infrastructure is introduced.

title: Fence Work Claims and Result Submission
description:
## Description

Implement simple authoritative work claims separately from campaign-controller authority. A configured actor ID and random per-start instance ID identify a claimant; advisory presence publishes only static capabilities and lease freshness. Presence may improve routing but never proves ownership or drives correctness.

Each work claim is its own S3 CAS domain. Claiming, renewal, reclamation, and submission all transition the same claim object so completion cannot race reclamation through a different key.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Stable actor identity and ephemeral instance identity are distinct, and every claim binds both identities, the work revision, and a monotonic fence.
- [ ] Presence contains actor, instance, static capabilities, and freshness only; stale or missing presence cannot violate ownership or block recovery.
- [ ] Claim creation, renewal, and reclamation use create-if-absent or `If-Match` on the same claim key, with one frozen lease policy and no generic membership or lease framework.
- [ ] Internal execute/submit APIs require an opaque fence-bearing claim authority value rather than accepting raw IDs supplied by a worker.
- [ ] Completion performs a same-key CAS from `ACTIVE(fence)` to `SEALED/SUBMITTED(fence, result_ref)`; reclamation and completion race on that ETag, and only one can win.
- [ ] A controller records only sealed submissions whose immutable result identity and work revision validate. A stale result may remain as evidence but cannot complete work.
- [ ] Two machines racing for a claim cannot both hold valid authority, and a lower-fence or wrong-revision submission fails closed.
- [ ] Unexpired claims remain valid across controller replacement and their sealed submissions can be processed by the replacement.
- [ ] Fault tests cover lost claim/renewal/submission responses, completion racing reclamation, worker death, a delayed old-fence return, and restart reconciliation without a machine-departure event.

title: Seal one E10 preflight receipt and execution schedule
description:
## Context

E10 runs the precommitted MVP feasibility experiment, so every execution input and validity rule must be fixed before the first result is visible. This task creates the minimum receipt needed to prove that the Research and Change pilots use E01's exact contract and that the eventual decision cannot drift after observation.

The receipt is not a new experiment framework. It is a compact set of immutable references plus the concrete execution schedule for the two pilots.

## Current State

The repository currently contains `docs/epics.md`, `docs/mvp-outline.md`, and beads metadata; it has no code or experiment artifacts. E01 is expected to produce the checked-in private pilot/precommit configuration. E02-E09 are expected to produce S3-chain, SQLite reconstruction, claim/controller fencing, Research, candidate, evaluator/process/provider/code-host, and Change artifacts and tests.

E10's contract is in `docs/epics.md:229-252`. Treatment shapes and measurements are in `docs/mvp-outline.md` §32; hard invariants and MVP completion rules are in §43 and §44.

## Desired State

One small, immutable preflight receipt references the authoritative E01 Git revision/content digests and the existing E02-E09 artifact, run, and owning-test identities. It validates the E01-frozen schedule, capture, timing, validity, and replacement rules (ravel-j4t) by revision/digest and seals only what E01 leaves open — concrete host identities, A/B/C host allocation, execution order, and the deterministic schedule-seed instantiation — before any E10 observation, without copying those artifacts into new manifests or inventories. E10 does not author or reseal timing, validity, replacement, or schedule rules after the E06/E09 live runs.

The receipt has an objective `READY` or `BLOCKED` result. A missing or mismatched required input cannot be replaced by operator choice.

## Implementation Guidance

- Follow the private experiment configuration/output convention established by E01. Do not introduce a public schema, migration system, experiment framework, or runtime module solely for this receipt.
- Reference E01 values by revision/digest rather than duplicating the Research question, Change repository/base/discovery rule, treatment definitions, bounds, run counts, model/provider profiles, evaluator commands, branch policy, scoring rules, or success criteria.
- Reference the immutable outputs and owning-test artifacts produced by E02-E09.
- Validate the E01-frozen treatment-application unit, analysis unit, reset/interference rules, timing boundaries, faulted-run placement, invalid-attempt validity/replacement rules, and treatment-neutral capture contract by revision/digest; seal only the E10-owned instantiation: A/B/C host allocation, execution order, and deterministic schedule seed. Record which reserved upstream treatment-C observations (qualifying `ravel-85q.8` / `ravel-e1n.7` runs) are consumed.
- Record at least three independent host identities and capabilities, required measurement captureability, and the existing fault hooks needed for distributed and composed-failure runs.
- Define separate fields for attempt status, evidence-validity verdict, and treatment outcome. Treatment outcome is populated only for evidence-valid attempts. Retain every attempt and seal the rule for counting or replacing invalid attempts.
- Seal this transition table: blocked preflight or invalid/incomplete execution yields no go/no-go and denies MVP completion; a valid `NO-GO` completes E10 but denies MVP completion; a valid `GO` completes E10 but permits MVP completion only when every mandatory gate is `PASS`.
- If allocation/order/reset/interference evidence cannot support a treatment-effect claim, require the final report to mark that question `INDETERMINATE`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The receipt resolves the exact E01 input revision and content digests for both workflows, all three treatments, frozen bounds/run counts, scoring rules, and success criteria. (E10 AC1)
- [ ] The receipt references the E01-frozen treatment-application/analysis units, reset/interference rules, timing boundaries, fault placement, and validity/replacement rules by revision/digest — authoring or resealing none of them — and records host allocation, execution order, and schedule seed before the first observation. (E10 AC1)
- [ ] At least three independent hosts and all required distributed capabilities pass preflight. (E10 AC2)
- [ ] Captureability is proven for every mandatory Research and Change measurement; a missing required field produces `BLOCKED`. (E10 AC4, AC5)
- [ ] Existing E02-E09 artifact/run/owning-test identities are referenced without copying them into a second evidence inventory. (E10 AC7)
- [ ] Attempt status, evidence validity, and treatment outcome are distinct, every attempt is retained, and the invalid-attempt counting/replacement rule is the E01-frozen rule, validated rather than defined here. (E10 AC1)
- [ ] Reserved upstream treatment-C observations (qualifying `ravel-85q.8` / `ravel-e1n.7` runs executed under the frozen capture contract) are validated and recorded as consumed C observations exactly once. (E10 AC1)
- [ ] The blocked/invalid/valid-no-go/valid-go/MVP-completion transition table is recorded exactly and cannot be edited after observation. (E10 AC10)
- [ ] Any missing or mismatched required precommit field, host capability, captureability check, or mandatory upstream identity yields `BLOCKED`; no substitute can be selected by an operator. (E10 AC10)
- [ ] No experiment framework, public configuration API, telemetry service, proof registry, or final evidence manifest is introduced. (E10 AC8 and explicit prohibitions)

## Testing Strategy

- **Unit/fixture:** Use a minimal valid receipt fixture plus missing/digest-mismatch cases; verify deterministic schedule generation from the recorded seed and fail-closed validation.
- **Integration:** Resolve real E01 and E02-E09 references, probe all three hosts, and verify required record fields and fault hooks are observable without running treatments.
- **Manual review:** Confirm that the receipt contains references rather than copied definitions, was sealed before observations, and has no operator-selectable fallback.

## Design Gate
Design settled by docs/mvp-outline.md §0, §43, §32, §33, §44; decomposed from epic ravel-4dw via forged plan /home/ahrav/.claude/plans/2026-08-08-ravel-e10-tasks-v2.md. No separate design review required.

## Final Step

- [ ] Run a /ponytail-review pass on the final work (remove over-engineering; simplest version that meets the acceptance criteria) before closing this task.
- [ ] Run a /doc-rigor pass on the final work (verify all docs/comments against source) before closing this task.

title: Execute the frozen Research treatment matrix
description:
## Context

E10 must compare the frozen Research treatments: one strong agent on one machine, multiple agents on one machine, and the distributed campaign. This task runs that matrix exactly as sealed and retains enough evidence to measure results and prove real autonomous multi-machine behavior.

The task exercises the Research pilot built by E06; it does not add Research workflow behavior or redefine the experiment.

## Current State

The repository currently has only design documents and beads metadata. Before this task can start, E01 must supply the frozen Research input, treatment definitions, bounds, run counts, scoring method, and success criteria; E02-E06 must supply the durable chain, reconstruction, fencing/controller, models, and Research workflow behavior. Step 1 supplies a `READY` preflight receipt and seeded schedule. The Research pilot has no oracle/evaluator role: E06 owns researchers, critics, the optional fixed adjudicator, and synthesis, and grading stays post-hoc per the closed ravel-q3w.2 contract.

The relevant design is `docs/mvp-outline.md` §0 and §32, with autonomy and completion rules in §43-§44.

## Desired State

title: Run the composed external-unknown-outcome recovery scenario
description:
## Context

E02-E09 prove individual durability, fencing, workflow, provider, process, evaluator, and code-host boundaries. E10 needs one final live scenario showing that those existing mechanisms compose when an active worker and controller fail around an external call whose result is unknown.

This is a bounded proof of the selected scenario, not a generic fault-injection or recovery framework.

## Current State

The repository currently has only design documents and beads metadata. By the time this task runs, prior epics must supply the S3 chain, claim/controller fencing, fresh SQLite reconstruction, operation identities, provider/code-host reconciliation, process cleanup, and workflow terminal-state machinery. Steps 2 and 3 must have completed the live pilot matrices on the preflighted hosts.

E10 AC3 defines the composed scenario. `docs/mvp-outline.md` §43 forbids unfenced completion, stale-controller commits, unreconciled side effects, exactly-once claims, and unbounded action chains; §44 requires real failover and no duplicate authoritative effect.

## Desired State

One valid, ordered, immutable three-host scenario trace proves that the selected external call crossed its boundary and lost its response, the active worker and controller were killed at the registered points, recovery reconstructed from a fresh durable head on another host, and stale authority could not publish after takeover.

Recovery ends within frozen bounds in one coherent completion or explicit `UNRESOLVED`. The scenario leaves the environment restored and has no duplicate authoritative effect.

## Implementation Guidance

- Reuse existing §42 modules and hooks, especially operation-local `recovery/reconcile.rs` (there is no generic `recovery/outbox.rs`; reconciliation stays operation-local), `sync/head.rs`, `sync/replay.rs`, `distributed/claims.rs`, `distributed/fencing.rs`, `distributed/controller.rs`, and `db/projections.rs`.
- Before injection, record: target campaign/run and external operation identity; expected worker/controller identities and fences; no-fault baseline; an injection oracle independent of the worker/controller under test; blast-radius exclusions; abort guardrails; restoration/cleanup procedure; and explicit invalidation criteria.
- Invalidation includes wrong target, failure to inject, missing independent witness, recovery starting before proven response loss, protocol deviation, or guardrail breach. Retain an invalid attempt but do not count it as a failed treatment/scenario outcome.
- Prove with existing immutable records that the external request crossed the boundary and that its response was lost before recovery began. Do not infer this merely from local absence.
- Kill the active worker around the call, then kill the active controller while the outcome remains unknown. Recover or promote authority on another host after fresh SQLite reconstruction and fresh-head verification.
- Use the owning operation-identity and complete retained-chain/remote-state reconciliation path. Reintroduce delayed stale worker/controller activity and verify fence rejection.
- Enforce frozen attempt/depth/deadline/cost bounds, cleanup process groups/resources, and restore the test environment. Do not claim exactly-once.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A pre-registered target manifest identifies the campaign, external operation, worker/controller identities and fences, hosts, injection points, and expected evidence. (E10 AC3)
- [ ] A no-fault baseline, independent injection oracle, blast-radius exclusions, abort guardrails, restoration path, and invalidation criteria are recorded before injection. (E10 AC3)
- [ ] Existing evidence independently proves the external call crossed the boundary and its response was lost before recovery started. (E10 AC3)
- [ ] On at least three independent hosts, the active worker and controller are killed at the registered points and recovery authority moves to another host. (E10 AC2, AC3)
- [ ] The replacement controller reconstructs SQLite from object storage and verifies the exact fresh durable head before authoritative action. (E10 AC2, AC3)
- [ ] Reconciliation uses operation identity plus complete retained-chain/remote-state evidence; absence from one local view is not treated as failure. (E10 AC3)
- [ ] Delayed stale worker and controller actions are rejected by their respective fences. (E10 AC3, AC10)
- [ ] Recovery remains within frozen bounds and ends in one coherent completion or explicit `UNRESOLVED`, with no duplicate authoritative effect or exactly-once claim. (E10 AC3, AC10)
- [ ] Invalid attempts are retained and replaced/counted only under the Step 1 sealed rule. (E10 AC1, AC3)
- [ ] Cleanup/restoration completes and the final durable chain and fresh projection agree on terminal state. (E10 AC3)

## Testing Strategy

- **Live baseline:** Run the same selected path without faults and retain its expected operation and terminal-state evidence.
- **Live fault integration:** Execute the registered worker/controller kills on real hosts and capture the independent oracle, immutable ordering, reconstruction, reconciliation, and stale-fence witnesses.
- **Validation:** Automatically reject a trace with a missed/wrong injection, missing boundary-crossing or response-loss proof, early recovery, guardrail violation, or inconsistent terminal state.
- **Manual review:** Verify blast radius, bounds, no exactly-once wording, environment restoration, and absence of duplicate authoritative effect.

## Design Gate

title: Implement the one offline renderer and score both workflows
description:
## Context

E10 needs comparable Research and Change measurements and a reproducible CSV/Markdown output, but the epic explicitly prohibits a telemetry product or general experiment framework. The smallest implementation is one offline renderer that is also the sole scoring and aggregation path.

This task converts retained immutable records into the two fixed tables required by the pilots. It does not change scoring rules or infer missing data.

## Current State

The repository currently has no code; by this task, E01 must provide the frozen scoring/outcome definitions and Steps 2-4 must provide retained Research, Change, and composed-scenario records. E02-E09 provide campaign events, provider usage, evaluator results, target/candidate identities, code-host records, and immutable traces.

Required measures are listed in E10 AC4/AC5 and `docs/mvp-outline.md` §32. E10 AC8 requires a small offline CSV/Markdown script and prohibits metrics services, dashboards, exporters, permanent baselines, adaptive reruns, and significance claims.

## Desired State

One small offline script reads the sealed receipt and retained records, applies only frozen E01 definitions, and emits deterministic CSV plus a Markdown report draft. It produces one fixed Research table and one fixed Change table, with provenance back to immutable identities.

The script is the only calculation path. Required missing data remains visible but causes a non-successful validation result and marks the affected criterion and experiment incomplete/invalid.

## Implementation Guidance

- Follow the E01 private experiment/output convention. The §42 runtime tree does not prescribe an E10 reporting module; do not add a daemon/runtime module, package, generic schema, plugin API, or service solely for this script.
- Read records from the existing durable/output formats. Do not create a second run index, evidence manifest, or independent aggregation/reconciliation implementation.
- Research table fields: run/treatment/validity identity, wall time, supported/incorrect/omitted/unresolved conclusions, useful evidence, discriminating follow-up, provider calls/tokens/usage/cost, duplicate work, scaling efficiency, and controller idle/bottleneck time.
- Change table fields: run/treatment/validity identity, correctly resolved targets, wall time, omissions, semantic corrections and candidate rejections, integration conflicts, wasted work, provider usage/cost per resolved target, worker utilization, scaling efficiency, and final rediscovery.
- Use E01's frozen denominators, timing boundaries, cost interpretation, and formulas. Include unfavorable valid treatment outcomes. List invalid attempts separately and apply only the sealed Step 1 count/replacement rule.
- Every aggregate must carry or resolve its source run/target/candidate/evaluator/code-host identities as applicable.
- Preserve an unavailable cell with its source-backed reason, but fail AC4/AC5 and mark the experiment incomplete/invalid for any required unavailable value. Never default, estimate, or drop it.
- Keep analysis descriptive. Do not add significance tests, confidence claims, causal claims, adaptive reruns, or result-dependent exclusions.
- Use a tiny smoke fixture and concise `--help`; do not add byte-for-byte CSV/Markdown golden snapshots or standalone usage documentation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] One offline invocation emits CSV and a Markdown report draft from retained records, with deterministic row and heading order. (E10 AC8)
- [ ] The Research table contains every required AC4 measure plus provider invocation and controller idle/bottleneck fields needed by §32/AC9. (E10 AC4, AC9)
- [ ] The Change table contains every required AC5 measure and final trusted rediscovery. (E10 AC5)
- [ ] Frozen E01 definitions are the only source for scoring, denominators, timing, cost, duplicate/wasted-work, utilization, and scaling calculations. (E10 AC1, AC4, AC5)
- [ ] Every valid scheduled Research/Change run appears exactly once; invalid attempts remain separately visible and are not scored as treatment outcomes. (E10 AC1)
- [ ] Every aggregate traces to immutable run/target/candidate/evaluator/code-host identities as applicable. (E10 AC4, AC5)
- [ ] A required unavailable Research or Change value is retained with its reason, causes validation failure, fails AC4/AC5, and marks the experiment incomplete/invalid. (E10 AC4, AC5, AC10)
- [ ] A tiny fixture checks required rows, columns, headings, totals, identities, missing-field failure, and deterministic ordering through the same production calculation path. (E10 AC8)
- [ ] The script provides concise `--help` and adds no golden snapshots, separate aggregation implementation, standalone usage guide, service, dashboard, exporter, permanent baseline, adaptive rerun, or statistical-significance machinery. (E10 AC8)

## Testing Strategy

- **Unit/fixture:** Run one tiny fixture through the real renderer and check required structure, known totals, identity propagation, ordering, duplicate-ID rejection, and missing-required-field failure.
- **Integration:** Run against the complete retained E10 record set; reconcile scheduled attempt identities, target denominators, provider usage, evaluator results, and final rediscovery.
- **Manual review:** Trace representative rows and every headline aggregate to immutable sources; scan output and code for post-hoc exclusions, alternate calculations, significance/causal language, and prohibited infrastructure.

title: Adjudicate autonomy and owning-correctness evidence in the final report
description:
## Context

E10 must prove that routine pilot progress was autonomous and reference the correctness evidence owned by earlier epics. To keep the gate small, these statuses belong directly in the final Markdown report's single gate checklist rather than in a separate proof packet or registry.

This task performs the focused autonomy and owning-evidence adjudication before the final §43/§44 decision.

## Current State

The repository currently has no code. By this task, E02-E09 must have produced owning tests and immutable artifacts for durability, projection, fencing, provider/process/evaluator/code-host boundaries; Steps 2-4 must have retained work/decision records, operator actions, and composed-failure evidence; Step 5 must have created the Markdown report draft.

E10 AC6 defines forbidden routine human control. AC7 names correctness evidence for S3 ambiguity, SQLite projection, claim/controller fencing, provider unknown outcomes, process cleanup, trusted evaluation, and code-host reconciliation.

## Desired State

The final report draft contains one gate checklist with objective autonomy rows and eight explicit correctness-mechanism rows. Each correctness row references the owning test and existing immutable artifact identity; no mechanism is reimplemented and no assertion-level registry is created.

Routine human intervention produces `FAIL`, not an omission or explanatory waiver. Missing owning evidence produces `MISSING` and remains visible for the final MVP gate.

## Implementation Guidance

- Update the final Markdown report draft emitted by Step 5. Do not create a standalone autonomy matrix, correctness index, proof packet, CI catalog, or assertion registry.
- Adjudicate autonomy using immutable campaign-created work, routing, judgment, decision, integration, and operator-action records from Steps 2-4.
- Allowed human inputs are the objective, constraints, policy, budget, and explicitly configured outer authority boundary. Post-run grading is measurement only.
- Mark AC6 `FAIL` if humans assigned routine work, approved routine conclusions, chose ordinary candidates, performed routine safe-branch integration, or extended routine bounds.
- Enumerate eight correctness mechanisms separately:
  1. S3 ambiguity.
  2. SQLite atomic projection.
  3. Claim fencing.
  4. Controller fencing.
  5. Provider unknown outcomes.
  6. Process cleanup.
  7. Trusted evaluation.
  8. Code-host reconciliation.
- For each mechanism, reference the owning E02-E09 test identity and its existing immutable artifact/run identity. Do not copy assertions or invent a new test in E10.
- Use only `PASS`, `FAIL`, or `MISSING`, with a short evidence reference/reason. Carry every non-pass state into Step 7.
- Relevant §42 ownership includes `storage/s3.rs`, `sync/`, `db/projections.rs`, `distributed/claims.rs`, `distributed/controller.rs`, `distributed/fencing.rs`, `models/`, `sandbox/process.rs`, `oracle/`, `code_host/`, and `recovery/reconcile.rs`; E10 only references their evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The final report directly classifies whether humans supplied only objective/configuration/outer-boundary authority. (E10 AC6)
- [ ] Any routine human work assignment, conclusion approval, ordinary candidate choice, safe-branch integration, or bound extension is an explicit `FAIL`. (E10 AC6)
- [ ] Claim fencing and controller fencing are separate rows, yielding eight correctness mechanisms in total. (E10 AC7)
- [ ] Each of the eight rows references its owning E02-E09 test and existing immutable artifact identity. (E10 AC7)
- [ ] No E10 substitute test, duplicated recovery mechanism, assertion-level registry, separate proof packet, or multi-matrix artifact is added. (E10 AC7 and explicit prohibitions)
- [ ] Every row uses `PASS`, `FAIL`, or `MISSING`, and every non-pass state is preserved for the final MVP-completion decision. (E10 AC10)
- [ ] References resolve to immutable artifacts and contain no secret material. (E10 AC7, AC10)

## Testing Strategy

- **Reference validation:** Resolve every owning-test and immutable-artifact identity and reject dangling, mutable, or duplicate references.
- **Fixture:** Use a tiny checklist fixture with one allowed human action, one forbidden routine action, and one missing artifact to prove `PASS`/`FAIL`/`MISSING` behavior.
- **Manual review:** Inspect operator and campaign records for unrecorded routine authority and confirm all eight mechanisms are independently represented without copied assertions.

title: Finalize the section 43/44 gate and issue the feasibility decision
description:
## Context

E10 exists to make the precommitted MVP feasibility decision, not merely to collect runs. This final task completes the single proof checklist, applies the decision table sealed before observation, and publishes the final CSV and Markdown report.

Experiment validity, the `GO`/`NO-GO` recommendation, E10 completion, and MVP completion remain separate outcomes. A valid `NO-GO` completes E10, while favorable performance can never override missing safety or definition-of-done evidence.

## Current State

The repository currently has no code. By this task, Step 5 must have emitted validated Research/Change tables, CSV, and a Markdown report draft; Step 6 must have populated autonomy and eight owning-correctness rows. E02-E09 and Steps 2-4 must supply immutable evidence for hard invariants, workflow behavior, real multi-machine execution, failover, and composed recovery.

The gate is defined by E10 AC9/AC10, `docs/mvp-outline.md` §43's twenty invariants, and every §44 definition-of-done requirement across distributed substrate, autonomous control, Research, Change, failure behavior, and measurement.

## Desired State

The final Markdown report contains one complete gate checklist, validated fixed measurement tables, an explicit experiment-validity status, an evidence-backed `GO` or `NO-GO` only when the experiment is valid, an E10-completion status, and an MVP-completion status.

Every checklist row is `PASS`, `FAIL`, or `MISSING` with an immutable reference. Any mandatory non-pass state denies MVP completion. The final report answers only the questions required by E10 AC9.

## Implementation Guidance

- Complete the same checklist started in Step 6; do not create additional invariant, distributed-proof, or definition-of-done matrices.
- Enumerate all twenty §43 invariants. Map each to an owning E02-E09 artifact or direct E10 run/scenario evidence; never infer an invariant merely from a terminal campaign state.
- Enumerate every §44 bullet under:
  - distributed substrate,
  - autonomous control,
  - Research,
  - Change,
  - failure behavior,
  - measurement.
- A §44 row may reference existing owning-epic evidence. Any `FAIL` or `MISSING` row denies MVP completion.
- Apply the Step 1 sealed transition table without edits:
  - `BLOCKED` or invalid/incomplete execution: no go/no-go, E10 incomplete, MVP denied.
  - Valid completed experiment yielding frozen `NO-GO`: E10 complete, MVP denied.
  - Valid `GO` with any mandatory AC6/AC7/AC10, §43, or §44 non-pass: E10 complete, MVP denied.
  - Valid `GO` with all mandatory rows `PASS`: E10 complete and MVP completion allowed.
- Answer only E10 AC9: where distribution helped, where scaling stopped, whether judge diversity and disagreement added value, what work was duplicated, and whether S3, controller, or evaluator paths were bottlenecks.
- Mark a treatment-effect answer `INDETERMINATE` when host/time/provider allocation, order, reset, or interference evidence cannot support it. Do not fill gaps with causal claims.
- Do not add general finding-trustworthiness, controller-created-work value, code-host bottleneck, or strongest-workflow ranking sections.
- Publish final CSV and Markdown using stable evidence references. Do not add a separate evidence manifest, dashboard, service, significance calculation, or secret data.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The final report contains every required Research and Change measurement; any required unavailable measure makes the experiment invalid/incomplete rather than merely caveated. (E10 AC4, AC5)
- [ ] The single gate checklist retains Step 6's autonomy and eight correctness rows and adds every one of the twenty §43 invariants. (E10 AC6, AC7, AC10)
- [ ] The checklist maps every §44 definition-of-done bullet across distributed substrate, autonomous control, Research, Change, failure behavior, and measurement. (E10 AC10)
- [ ] Every mandatory row is `PASS`, `FAIL`, or `MISSING` with an immutable owning-epic or E10 reference; any `FAIL`/`MISSING` denies MVP completion. (E10 AC10)
- [ ] The report proves actual three-host execution, late join, worker loss, controller failover, remote roles, fresh reconstruction, stale-authority rejection, and composed external-outcome recovery or explicit unresolved state. (E10 AC2, AC3, AC10)
- [ ] `GO` or `NO-GO` is issued only for a valid completed experiment and follows the frozen E01 criteria without reruns, exclusions, or threshold changes. (E10 AC9, AC10)
- [ ] A valid `NO-GO` is marked as completed E10 work but cannot mark the MVP complete. (E10 AC10)
- [ ] A valid `GO` marks the MVP complete only when every mandatory AC6/AC7/AC10, §43, and §44 row is `PASS`. (E10 AC10)
- [ ] The report answers only the AC9 scaling, judge-diversity/disagreement, duplication, and S3/controller/evaluator bottleneck questions; unsupported effects are `INDETERMINATE`. (E10 AC9)
- [ ] Final CSV/Markdown aggregates trace to immutable records, contain no secrets, and include no significance/confidence/unsupported causal claim or prohibited telemetry/framework artifact. (E10 AC8, AC9)

## Testing Strategy

- **Automated validation:** Reject missing checklist rows, unsupported statuses, unresolved references, missing required measures, duplicate run identities, or a decision inconsistent with the sealed transition table.
- **Fixture:** Exercise the table with blocked, invalid, valid-no-go, valid-go-with-missing-proof, and valid-go-all-pass cases.
- **Live evidence check:** Resolve representative and mandatory references through the durable chain, host/fault records, owning tests, and composed scenario.
- **Manual review:** Trace every narrative answer to the fixed tables, verify all §43/§44 rows, confirm AC9-only scope, and scan for post-hoc changes, secret leakage, significance/confidence language, unsupported causality, or an exactly-once claim.

## Design Gate

title: Synthesize with provenance closure and bounded completion
description:
## Context

E06 is complete only when bounded distributed observations become one coherent, auditable answer without a routine human approval step. The report must account for accepted and rejected claims, evidence, material objections, decisions, uncertainty, and unresolved items without allowing the synthesizer to invent authority or more work.

This task adds one synthesis invocation, deterministic provenance closure, and the fixed completion transition. It validates identifiers and evidence eligibility rather than trying to build a semantic truth detector.

## Current State

The repository currently has no implementation. `docs/mvp-outline.md` §17 requires conclusions, supporting evidence, rejected explanations, material uncertainty, unresolved questions, and bounded autonomous completion. `docs/epics.md` E06 requires full provenance and no routine human approval. §42 names workflow, decision, judgment, event, schema, and projection modules.

Steps 1-6 provide the two providers, immutable invocation records, direct Research admission, owned invocation lifecycle, initial/critic observations, fixed evidence decisions, and the optional sole discriminating item.

## Desired State

Once initial Research, the critic round, and any sole discriminating item are terminal under the fixed table, direct Research admission creates exactly one synthesis item. The synthesis call uses the same reservation, manifest/trace, cancellation, reconciliation, and supervisor path as every other model call. If fixed budget/deadline limits prevent model-synthesis admission, no provider call is made: the workflow instead emits exactly one deterministic non-model exhausted report built from eligible immutable decisions, evidence, and unresolved IDs, with the same five sections and the same provenance-closure validation.

The persisted report contains exactly five semantic sections: supported conclusions, evidence for each conclusion, rejected explanations, material uncertainty, and unresolved questions. It contains no `suggested next workflow` field and cannot spawn work.

A deterministic closure validator requires every eligible accepted/rejected claim ID, material-objection ID, decision ID, and unresolved-item ID to appear exactly once in report accounting sets. Every conclusion evidence reference resolves to eligible immutable evidence, and every work/attempt/request/provider/model/profile/manifest/trace provenance link resolves. Missing, duplicate, dangling, or stale-audit-only references fail validation. The validator does not decide whether prose is true; the fixed decision table owns acceptance.

The controller completes autonomously when all required questions are synthesized and no material contradiction is unaccounted for, or when fixed budget/deadline exhaustion made every unresolved ID explicit. Synthesis cannot reopen criticism, create a follow-up, or require a human accept button.

## Implementation Guidance

- Extend `src/workflows/research/` for synthesis admission, validation, and completion; use `src/domain/judgment.rs`, `src/domain/decision.rs`, `src/sync/event.rs`, `src/db/schema.rs`, and `src/db/projections.rs` from §42.
- Add synthesis-specific state/counters only now. Atomically debit its applicable work and invocation limits before creating/dispatching it.
- Build the synthesis input from eligible immutable observations and fixed decisions only. Exclude every stale work revision and claim fence observation; controller-fence provenance alone does not exclude an otherwise-eligible observation. Commit the synthesis decision and completion events under current controller authority through the fenced path.
- Use closed sets/maps keyed by stable IDs for the closure check. Compare expected and reported ID sets exactly; reject omission, duplication, or unknown IDs.
- Resolve all conclusion evidence and provenance references against immutable artifacts/events. Do not attempt model-based unsupported-conclusion detection or infer omitted uncertainty from prose.
- The output schema contains the five E06 sections only. Delete the future-facing `suggested next workflow` field and any behavior/test that creates work from it.
- Commit completion through the fenced controller and fixed Research table. Completion is replayable and does not depend on SQLite-only state or human approval.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Exactly one synthesis item is produced, only after all required prior phases are terminal under the fixed stopping rule: either one admitted model synthesis or, when limits prevent admission, one deterministic non-model exhausted report (no provider call) — never zero, never both. **(E06 AC 5, 9)**
- [ ] Synthesis uses the same charged, traced, reconciled, supervisor-owned invocation state machine as research and critic calls. **(E06 AC 2, 3, 5, 10)**
- [ ] The final report contains supported conclusions, evidence per conclusion, rejected explanations, material uncertainty, and unresolved questions. **(E06 AC 9)**
- [ ] Every eligible accepted/rejected claim, material objection, decision, and unresolved ID is accounted for exactly once. **(E06 AC 9)**
- [ ] Every conclusion evidence/provenance reference resolves to eligible immutable evidence and complete work/attempt/request/provider/model/profile/manifest/trace identity. **(E06 AC 2, 4, 9)**
- [ ] Missing, duplicate, dangling, unknown, or stale-audit-only references fail validation without semantic truth heuristics. **(E06 AC 4, 9)**
- [ ] Clean, resolved-disagreement, and budget/deadline-exhausted workflows complete deterministically without routine human approval. **(E06 AC 5, 9)**
- [ ] Synthesis has no `suggested next workflow`, cannot reopen criticism, and cannot create another follow-up or exceed a bound. **(E06 AC 5, 8, 11)**

## Testing Strategy

- **Fixture:** valid clean report, resolved-disagreement report, and budget-exhausted report with explicit unresolved IDs produced by the deterministic non-model fallback (no provider call made).
- **Unit:** exact ID-set closure, evidence eligibility, complete provenance resolution, omission, duplicate, dangling, and stale-reference rejection.
- **Invocation integration:** prove synthesis receives a manifest/start/terminal trace and is joined/reaped by the supervisor on interruption.
- **Replay:** rebuild the same final report reference and completion state from durable history.
- **Manual review:** confirm only the five required sections exist, no semantic truth detector was added, and no human approval/future-work behavior is required.

## Design Gate

title: Prove the three-host Research pilot and audit E06
description:
## Context

E06's central proof cannot be satisfied by unit tests or several subprocesses on one workstation. The concrete Research pilot must run on at least three independent machines/VM hosts, survive a late join, worker loss, controller takeover, stale returns, and one representative provider/process interruption, then autonomously produce a provenance-complete bounded result.

This task retains the campaign evidence and performs the final E06 audit. It reuses the concrete pilot and prior lifecycle tests rather than creating an orchestration product, conformance framework, fake provider API, or six-point live fault matrix.

## Current State

The repository currently has no implementation or retained pilot run. `docs/epics.md` E06 requires three-host concurrency, late-join reconstruction, worker reclaim, controller failover, stale-result rejection, interruption reconciliation/reaping, autonomous synthesis, and all explicit abstraction prohibitions. `docs/mvp-outline.md` §§31 and 44 require actual multi-machine execution/failover; §42 names the workflow, controller, claims, fencing, replay, and reconciliation modules.

E01 is expected to supply the selected providers/profiles, S3 environment, pilot question, trust boundaries, and fixed bounds. E02-E05 supply the same node binary's S3 log/projection, claims, controller fences, and supervisor. Steps 1-7 supply the complete concrete Research workflow.

## Desired State

One retained campaign runs the same binary on at least three independent hosts and proves:

- initial Research attempts overlap across hosts;
- critic attempts overlap and the total Research/critic work is executed by at least three independent hosts;
- a fresh host joins with no copied SQLite state, rebuilds from S3 to the verified head, claims work, and contributes an eligible accepted submission;
- a worker disappears with active work, a higher claim fence reclaims it, and its delayed stale response remains audit-only;
- controller authority moves to another host after rebuilding the exact fresh head, without losing committed observations or accepting stale-controller output. A worker holding an unchanged, unexpired claim across that takeover returns its result and the replacement controller accepts and commits it, while the old controller's own transitions are rejected;
- one representative provider/process interruption is reconciled by request identity or becomes explicit unresolved, and all local handles are joined/reaped;
- hard limits remain within their fixed charges and final synthesis completes autonomously with full provenance.

The retained artifacts are sufficient for a manual checklist against all eleven E06 criteria. Static architecture review confirms exactly two adapters, one concrete `workflows::research` module, and none of the prohibited frameworks.

## Implementation Guidance

- Exercise the §42 paths `src/workflows/research/`, `src/controller/scheduler.rs`, `src/distributed/controller.rs`, `src/distributed/claims.rs`, `src/distributed/fencing.rs`, `src/sync/replay.rs`, and `src/recovery/reconcile.rs`.
- Use the actual E01-selected providers/profiles and S3 campaign. Hosts must be independent machines/VMs, not three processes or containers sharing one host identity.
- Record stable actor and ephemeral instance identities, host evidence, work/attempt/request IDs, provider/model/profile, claim/controller fences, event heads/cursors, and time/overlap evidence.
- Start the late joiner without copied SQLite. Require it to rebuild from durable S3 history, verify the current head, then claim and submit ordinary work.
- Remove or stop one worker without a departure event; wait for ordinary lease expiry/reclaim and capture the higher fence plus stale-return exclusion.
- Transfer controller authority using E02-E05's fenced path. The replacement rebuilds to the fresh head before its first decision.
- Inject one representative interruption, preferably remote success with lost local response or local process interruption during waiting. Reuse Step 4's deterministic lifecycle fault suite for exhaustive cuts; do not reproduce six distributed interruption cases.
- Retain manifests, terminal traces/unresolved records, decisions, limit charges, unresolved IDs, supervisor/reap evidence, and final report. Produce a simple evidence checklist, not a generic conformance framework.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Retained identity evidence proves at least three independent machines/VM hosts executed overlapping initial Research and critic attempts. **(E06 AC 6)**
- [ ] A host starting without copied SQLite rebuilds to the verified S3 head, claims work, and contributes an eligible accepted submission. **(E06 AC 6)**
- [ ] Worker disappearance requires no departure event; higher-fence reclaim succeeds and the old response is retained only as audit data. **(E06 AC 7)**
- [ ] Controller authority moves hosts only after a fresh-head rebuild, preserving committed progress and rejecting stale-controller transitions. **(E06 AC 7)**
- [ ] A worker with an unchanged, unexpired claim spanning the controller takeover has its result accepted and committed by the replacement controller; controller-fence provenance alone does not invalidate it. **(E06 AC 7)**
- [ ] If this run consumes the reserved E01 treatment-C observation slot, it executes under the frozen E01 capture contract (ravel-j4t) and records the reserved C run ID and required measurement records; otherwise it is proof-only and E10 runs the C observation separately.
- [ ] One representative provider/process interruption ends in request-identity reconciliation or explicit unresolved state, with no unjoined local task or unreaped child. **(E06 AC 3, 10)**
- [ ] Retained charges prove calls/tokens, attempts, parallelism, critic work, adjudication when used, follow-up count/depth, and deadline never exceed E01 bounds. **(E06 AC 5)**
- [ ] Material disagreement creates at most one evidence-driven discriminating item before synthesis. **(E06 AC 8)**
- [ ] Final synthesis is autonomous, coherent after join/loss/takeover, contains all five required sections, and has complete eligible provenance. **(E06 AC 9)**
- [ ] Every call in the retained run has a separate manifest and terminal trace or explicit terminal unresolved record. **(E06 AC 2)**
- [ ] The final audit confirms exactly two internal providers, one fixed Research decision table, and one concrete `workflows::research` module, with no public provider API, agent harness, profile registry, generic scheduler policy, policy engine, adjudication platform, workflow trait, or DSL. **(E06 AC 1, 4, 11)**

## Testing Strategy

- **Live integration:** execute the retained three-host campaign with the selected providers and S3 environment; capture overlap, identities, heads, fences, and accepted submissions.
- **Fault injection:** one bounded live provider/process interruption plus worker disappearance and controller takeover; rely on Step 4 unit/fixture coverage for exhaustive invocation cuts.
- **Artifact audit:** verify manifests/traces, budget charges, decisions, unresolved IDs, provenance closure, supervisor evidence, and final report against the durable log.
- **Manual review:** complete an eleven-criterion E06 checklist and static source search for every prohibited abstraction.
- **No new framework:** keep scripts/fixtures specific to the pilot and selected adapters; do not add a generic orchestration or conformance product.

## Design Gate

title: Define the minimal Change protocol projection
description:
## Context

E09 (`ravel-e1n`) needs a concrete `workflows::change` protocol that can compose the already-owned candidate, evaluation, judgment, and integration paths without collapsing their meanings. This task creates the minimum durable Change state needed for later discovery, work creation, terminal accounting, and autonomous stopping.

The pilot is intentionally concrete. Change must not become a workflow DSL or copy the lifecycle records owned by E06–E08.

## Current State

The repository currently has design documents and beads metadata but no code. `docs/epics.md` defines E09’s required lifecycle separation, and `docs/mvp-outline.md` §§16 and 18 define the concrete Change protocol. The suggested paths are in §42.

This task builds on the durable event/projector and scheduler substrate and on prior-epic outputs from E06 (`ravel-85q`), E07 (`ravel-amn`), and E08 (`ravel-6hv`). Those epics own attempt, candidate, evaluation, judgment, Git, and code-host integration records. E01 (`ravel-q3w`) owns the private fixed pilot configuration.

## Desired State

`pi-campaign/src/workflows/change/` exists as a concrete module. Durable Change state contains only:

- workflow input, declared base epoch, and fixed pilot configuration references;
- the target ledger and target provenance required by E09;
- deterministic group membership and the emitted work reference;
- one terminal target disposition with reason/provenance;
- the final-discovery observation and workflow stop result; and
- stable references to E06–E08 attempt, candidate, evaluation, judgment, and integration records.

Change does not copy those prerequisite records. Change does own one closed, Change-local transition table — fixed data, not a framework — mapping every observed outcome class to exactly one retry decision or one terminal target disposition: candidate-less attempt; sandbox/delta rejection; evaluator `FAIL`, `ERROR`, and `TIMEOUT`; semantic rejection; write-scope/integration conflict; terminal non-integration; budget/deadline exhaustion. No row may leave targets indefinitely pending. Queries can independently distinguish attempt completion, candidate existence, evaluation eligibility, semantic acceptance, integration observation, and terminal target disposition.

## Implementation Guidance

Use `pi-campaign/src/workflows/change/` for concrete Change-owned types and projection logic. Extend only the necessary rows/constraints in `pi-campaign/src/db/schema.rs` and `pi-campaign/src/db/projections.rs`. Reuse stable identities from `pi-campaign/src/domain/work.rs`, `attempt.rs`, `evaluation.rs`, `judgment.rs`, and `decision.rs` as they are established by prerequisite epics.

Apply Change events through the existing durable-history projection path. Preserve its duplicate-event, ordering, and fail-closed behavior. Keep uniquely durable state out of SQLite. Do not add an online migration framework, generic projector, workflow trait, workflow registry, or universal target type.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A concrete `workflows::change` module represents workflow input/base/config references, targets, groups, target terminal dispositions, final discovery, and stop result.
- [ ] Change-owned persistence stores references to existing attempt, candidate, evaluation, judgment, and integration records rather than duplicating their payloads or statuses.
- [ ] Attempt completion, candidate identity, evaluation eligibility, semantic acceptance, integration state, and terminal target disposition are independently queryable and no earlier fact implies a later fact.
- [ ] Replaying durable history into a fresh local projection reconstructs identical Change state; duplicate application is a no-op and invalid ordering fails closed under the existing projector contract.
- [ ] The schema contains only E09-required rows and integrity constraints and leaves no uniquely durable state in SQLite.
- [ ] A closed Change-local transition table covers candidate-less attempt, sandbox/delta rejection, evaluator `FAIL`/`ERROR`/`TIMEOUT`, semantic rejection, write-scope/integration conflict, terminal non-integration, and budget/deadline exhaustion; every row yields exactly one retry decision or terminal disposition, with exhaustiveness enforced by the type system (no wildcard match).
- [ ] No workflow trait, DSL, registry, universal `Target`, or schema-migration framework is introduced.

## Testing Strategy

Use unit/projection tests with a fixed event fixture. Replay it into fresh databases and compare all Change queries. Include states for completed attempt without candidate, candidate without eligibility, eligible candidate pending judgment, accepted candidate pending integration, integration pending reconciliation, and terminal target disposition. Reapply events to prove idempotence and inject stale/out-of-order references to prove fail-closed behavior. Use manual diff review to confirm prerequisite lifecycle records were referenced rather than copied.

## Design Gate
